documents.abstract: Wang, Lawrence K. 王抗曝 (2026). Dragon² (龖): From Mahjong's "Double Dragon Embrace" to Peaceful U.S.–China Coexistence and Peace Under Heaven-- A Life-Writing Narrative 《龖(Dragon²): 從麻將「雙龍抱」到中美和平共存與天下太平的生命書寫》. Evolutionary Progress in Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics. Lenox Institute Press, Massachusetts, USA. 8(10L), 43 pages. ........ ABSTRACT: 本文延續作者對「囍—𩺰—龖」的文化思考,將古字「龖」重新詮釋為 Dragon²(亦寫作 Dragon2)。囍象徵新婚之喜,𩺰象徵夫妻無論順境逆境皆相伴一生;龖則將關懷由家庭延伸至世界。在本文所採用的麻將規則中,「雙龍抱」指由兩對相同順子構成的組合,共含四副順子,每對中的兩副順子花色與數序相同。作者借其「抱而不鬥」的意象,將兩龍比喻為具有全球影響力的中國與美國,寄託兩國相互尊重、和平共存的願望。這是作者提出的跨文化和平隱喻,並非將龍視為美國固有的國家象徵。作者於龍年出生於中國,1949年遷至臺灣,後赴美求學、成家與工作。中國承載其出生、文化與早年記憶,臺灣見證其成長與求學,美國則承載其深造、事業與家庭生活。這段跨越海峽與太平洋的生命歷程,使中美關係成為與自身及家人命運相連的切身議題。本文比較「雙龍爭珠」「雙龍戲珠」「雙龍抱」與「雙龍護珠」的意象:若明珠代表霸權,兩龍可能陷入零和競爭;若明珠代表地球,兩龍便肩負共同守護的責任。文章進一步借用工程系統中的回饋、穩定與失控概念,闡述核戰無真正贏家的警示,主張中美競而不戰、強而有制、和而不同,並在氣候變遷、公共衛生、人工智慧安全與核風險降低等領域推動合作。和平的意義亦須落實於平民百姓的生活,使家庭免於戰亂、人民安居樂業、世代得以延續。「龖」為既有古漢字,由兩個繁體「龍」左右並列而成。本文賦予其「雙龍抱,雙吉祥,共築人間仙境」的文化新意,以兩龍相擁、彼此尊重,象徵雙重吉祥、和諧共存與天下太平。此一意涵及其中的中美合作寓意,均屬作者的現代文化詮釋,而非「龖」字的傳統字典釋義; 關鍵詞:龖;Dragon²;Dragon2;雙龍抱;麻將文化;囍;𩺰;中美關係;生命書寫;系統工程;核風險降低;世界和平;和諧共存;天下太平;雙重吉祥;平民福祉;中美合作; ABSTRACT: This article continues the author's cultural reflections on the sequence 囍–𩺰–龖, reinterpreting the ancient Chinese character 龖 as Dragon² (also written as Dragon2). 囍 symbolizes the joy of marriage, while 𩺰 represents lifelong companionship through prosperity and adversity. 龖 extends this concern from the family to the world. In the mahjong rules adopted here, "Double Dragon Embrace" consists of two pairs of identical sequences—four sequences in total, with the two sequences in each pair matching in both suit and numerical order. Drawing on the image of "embracing rather than fighting," the author uses the two dragons as a metaphor for China and the United States, two globally influential powers, expressing the hope that they will respect each other and coexist peacefully. This is a cross-cultural metaphor for peace proposed by the author, not a claim that the dragon is a traditional national symbol of the United States. Born in China in the Year of the Dragon, the author moved to Taiwan in 1949 and later pursued further education, established a family, and developed his career in the United States. China holds his birthplace, cultural roots, and early memories; Taiwan shaped his upbringing and education; and the United States became the setting for his advanced studies, career, and family life. This life journey across the Taiwan Strait and the Pacific makes U.S.–China relations a deeply personal concern connected to his own and his family's future. The article compares four images: "Two Dragons Contending for a Pearl," "Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl," "Double Dragon Embrace," and "Two Dragons Protecting a Pearl." If the pearl represents hegemony, the dragons may become trapped in zero-sum competition; if it represents the Earth, they share a responsibility to protect it. Drawing further on the engineering concepts of feedback, stability, and loss of control, the article emphasizes that nuclear war has no true winners. It advocates competition without warfare, strength exercised with restraint, and harmony without uniformity, alongside cooperation on climate change, public health, artificial intelligence safety, and nuclear risk reduction. Peace must also take concrete form in the lives of ordinary people, allowing families to live free from war, communities to thrive, and future generations to flourish. The character 龖 consists of two traditional Chinese 龍 characters placed side by side. The author gives it a new cultural meaning: "Two dragons embrace, bringing paired blessings and together creating an earthly paradise." Their embrace and mutual respect symbolize shared auspiciousness, harmonious coexistence, and peace under heaven. These meanings, including the association with U.S.–China cooperation, are the author's contemporary cultural interpretation rather than traditional dictionary definitions of 龖. KEYWORDS: 龖; Dragon²; Dragon2; Double Dragon Embrace; mahjong culture; 囍; 𩺰; U.S.–China relations; life writing; systems engineering; nuclear risk reduction; world peace; harmonious coexistence; peace under heaven; paired blessings; well-being of ordinary people; U.S.–China cooperation

Intelligent automation is now used to retrieve information, predict, recommend, generate content, route workflows and take physical or administrative action. Human-in-the-loop (HITL) design is often suggested as a possible fail-safe but it does not necessarily mean that a person is always in control. Oversight can be undermined by lack of time, authority, competence, independent evidence, or feedback or by a lack of real accountability despite the title of oversight. In this paper we explore HITL intelligent automation from three intertwined perspectives: calibrated trust, operational oversight, and workforce implications. It combines existing human-automation research, guidance for human–AI interaction, risk-management standards, regulation, and evidence of labor. A threat model encompasses technical misfortune, adversarial manipulation, cognitive and organizational failure, and harmful deployment of workforce. The mathematical formulation determines the automation modes based on expected error consequence, uncertainty, review cost, workload and skill preservation. The suggested architecture is that of separating the execution of the model from the risk routing, human decision making, dual authorization, audit, appeal, and learning feedback. A seeded synthetic experiment with 10,000 binary decisions is conducted for the comparisons between automation-only, passive universal review, risk-adaptive HITL, and dual control. With the declared generator, adaptive review achieves a 83.6% to 85.0% accuracy rate, while reviewing 37.1% of cases, and dual control achieves a 87.0% accuracy rate with a 5.2% rate of high impact error. These are indicative values and not measurements taken in the workplace. The review finds that effective HITL systems must have meaningful intervention capability, calibrated reliance, representative evaluation, protected worker voice, continuous competence and evidence of oversight functioning under realistic workload and failure.

documents.abstract: This study investigated the relationship between technological, process, and product innovation and employee productivity among employees of selected private higher education institutions (HEIs) in Laoag City, Philippines. It also examined whether age, sex, educational attainment, job tenure, and nature of work moderated the innovation–productivity relationship and developed a strategic action plan for institutional utilization of the findings. The participants were 271 full-time academic and non-academic employees from selected private HEIs. The findings showed that the institutions reported high levels of technological, process, and product innovation and high employee productivity. Process innovation had the strongest positive and statistically significant relationship with employee productivity, while technological innovation had a statistically significant but weaker positive relationship. Product innovation did not have a statistically significant relationship with employee productivity. None of the demographic characteristics significantly moderated the innovation–productivity relationship. The study recommends institutionalizing feasible policies for process innovation, strengthening technology utilization and responsible artificial intelligence integration, refining academic programs through Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence in Research Methods, and establishing participatory and governance mechanisms that can sustain innovation within existing institutional resources.

The library profession has evolved from being traditional bookkeepers to being modern end users of digital data and Artificial Intelligence (AI), over the years. But throughout development, libraries are facing a major crisis: a severe shortage of permanent staff. Administrative bodies are hiring outsourced and temporary staff for most of their work to maintain daily functions as much as possible. This paper critically evaluates the trend of contract hiring, under the title “Stability of Tenure: is contractualization a cure? “However, contract hiring may be a fast & temporary remedy to the problem of vacant positions, but it is disaster to the core essence of the library profession. The libraries need highly skilled, permanent experts to manage complex tasks, relying on temporary staff risks the dignity of profession and user trust. The paper concludes by urging policymakers to invest in stable, permanent jobs to protect the future of libraries.

Large language model (LLM) based software agents are transitioning from one shot assistants to long term actors that plan, negotiate and accomplish tasks with multiple services. This transformation is resulting in what researchers call the Agent Internet, the Agentic Web or the Internet of Agents, in which programs are full-fledged players alongside people. This article summarizes academic surveys, industry studies and public market data from 2025 to 2026 to outline the multi-layered nature of this setup and to consider its pros and cons. According to market estimates, the revenue for agent software is estimated to be around eight billion dollars in 2025 and up to 35-53 billion dollars in 2030. Adoption statistics tell a tale of much experimentation and few pilots taking it to scale. We discuss communication protocols that enable agents to find and trust each other, the as yet undeveloped identity and payment layers and the burden of agent traffic on advertising supported content. But the challenges that we see are not just capabilities, but security, accountability, interoperability, and who pays for content and compute. Finally, we highlight some of the current research and policy gaps and suggest avenues for a responsible construction.

documents.abstract: Abstract Agile teams depend on collaboration, collective learning, and shared accountability to function effectively. As team members increasingly use generative AI (GenAI) tools, these foundational dynamics may be disrupted. In this study, we investigate how individual human–AI collaboration affects agile teamwork through thirteen interviews with software and technology professionals. Our findings show that GenAI reshapes team collaboration and learning while enabling individuals to work across traditional role boundaries, but also reinforces the continued necessity of human oversight and team accountability. We argue that these dynamics challenge the notion of agile teams, and call for updated models of agile teamwork.

アブストラクト 二大政党得票率 $R_{k}=\frac{1}{2}(1+m_{k}^{*}/q_{k}^{*})$ を逆転させることが確認された。2018〜2020年のねじれ議会に対する歴史的バックテストからは、上院による制度的緩衝作用と急速な記憶散逸が、高投票率かつ順序可換な均衡($q_{k}^{*}>84\%$)を維持することが確認される。対照的に、緩衝作用のない両院の膠着状態の下では、最終的な選挙結果はショックの到達順序、ショック間の緩和間隔、州レベルの産業サプライチェーンのエクスポージャー、およびアーカイブ化されたスキャンダル開示の累積的範囲に依存すると仮説した。 従来の選挙競争に関する統計力学的モデルは、一般に二値イジングスピン仕様($s_{i}\in\{+1,-1\}$)に依拠しているが、これは一定の投票参加恒等式($s_{i}^{2}\equiv1$)を課すものであり、外生的な政策ショックや評判ショックが直接的なイデオロギーの転向のみを通じて選挙結果を変化させることを前提としている。この制約を緩和し、有権者の戦略的棄権($s_{i}=0$)を内生化するため、本研究では米国50州の空間ネットワーク上に、多項ロジット型量子応答均衡(QRE)と結合した3状態スピン1 Blume–Capel選挙ポテンシャルゲームを定式化する。各州において、有権者は非妥協的な党派的コア層と、反応性を有する3つの社会経済的階層(労働者階級および企業同調層の有権者、制度的エスタブリッシュメント層の有権者、ならびに真実追求型の無党派有権者)に分割される。水平磁場は、縦断的な世論調査および抗議活動の時系列データ(2024年12月〜2026年10月)から較正された純党派的政策格差を捉え、結晶場は純粋な市民参加インセンティブから多争点にわたる制度的シニシズムを差し引いたものを表す。解析的な6次ランダウ自由エネルギー展開により、中間選挙後の立法府の膠着状態と多争点政策ショックによってある階層の結晶場が対称三重臨界スピノーダル閾値($D_{t}/J_{\mathrm{eff}}=-\ln(4)/3\approx-0.4621$)を下回ると、2次および4次のランダウ係数の符号が反転し($a_{2}>0, a_{4}<0$)、磁化ゼロにおける常磁性的な棄権のポテンシャル井戸が安定化することが示される。大規模なベクトル化モンテカルロ・シミュレーション(24の歴史的および反事実的レジームにわたり、各レジームあたり$1.0\times10^{6}$から$1.2\times10^{6}$試行)により、交差圧力に晒された階層における選択的棄権が、純党派磁化の分子($m$)よりも速く有効投票率の分母($q$)を縮小させ、直接的な党派的離反を伴うことなく実効厳密な4次ビンダー・キュムラント分解($U_{4,k}$)および1次ソボル感度指数($S_{1,k}(X_{0})<10^{-5}$)により、初期事前分布に対する不変性が検証されるとともに、非対称的な投票ロックインと3階層全体の参加崩壊とを隔てる相境界が特定される。 研究背景 過去30年間にわたり世界のサイバーセキュリティ基盤を支えてきた「人間のオペレーターが有する時間および認知資源の希少性」という経済学的前提は、自律型人工知能(AI)および合成知能(SI: Synthetic Intelligence)エージェント群(Swarm)の実戦投入によって根底から崩壊した。脱獄(jailbreak)されたオープンウェイトモデルとオープンソースのエージェント・ハーネスを結合させることで、偵察、ゼロデイ脆弱性の発見、および多段階の侵入プロセスは完全に自動化され、企業1社あたりの侵害限界費用は約50〜100ドルという極小水準にまで低下している。実際に、複数の商用・オープンモデル(Claude、Grok、Kimi、および改変されたPentestGPT基盤等)を並行稼働させ、認可されたレッドチーム演習を装うことで安全ガードレールを突破し、中南米の銀行・金融機関400社以上やアルゼンチンの医療機関少なくとも15組織に自動侵入した事案や、インターネット上に公開されたAIゲートウェイおよびModel Context Protocol(MCP)サーバーを乗っ取り最大10万回の自動操作を試みる「LLMjacking」が観測されている。この構造変化は2026年10月(「Black October」)にスーパーエージェント主導の脆弱性カスケードとして顕在化した。世界のWebバックエンドの約70%を支えるPHPにおいて、数十年間潜在していた致命的な遠隔コード実行(RCE)脆弱性(CVE-2026-109618およびCVE-2026-109619、通称「PHP2Shell」、CVSS 9.2、ならびに後続のCVE-2026-115560)がAI支援のソースコード監査によって露呈すると、公開直後に数百万件規模の自動悪用試行が発生し、ペイロードをリアルタイムに変異させる攻撃によって、日本の地方銀行約20行や英国の32の行政サービスをはじめとする世界中のシステムが緊急停止(ロックダウン)を余儀なくされた。さらに同時期に、Node.js(CVE-2026-111497、「Node2Shell」)、JavaおよびGraalVM(CVE-2026-91403、CVSS 9.1)、GitLab(CVSS 10.0)、LinuxカーネルのSMBサーバー機能KSMBD(修正前に公開された2件のCVSS 9.0脆弱性)といった基幹ソフトウェアの欠陥や、週2,300万回ダウンロードされるAI開発ツールLiteLLMのサプライチェーン汚染、クラウド基盤(Railwayおよび32万1,810アカウントが露呈し事業閉鎖に至ったZeabur)の侵害が連鎖的に発生しており、AIがハードウェアレベルを含む未知の脆弱性を発見する速度は、人間によるパッチ適用とシステム改修の限界をすでに凌駕している。 こうした自律型攻撃の激化は、サイバー犯罪の形態を従来の「データ暗号化による身代金要求」から「金融市場の取引メカニズムを直接悪用した顧客資産の破壊と企業恐喝」へと変質させ、国家経済およびコーポレート・ガバナンスを根底から揺るがしている。日本国内では、GMOインターネットグループが提供するFX自動売買用仮想デスクトップ環境「お名前.com デスクトップクラウド」(最大2万6,739台のサーバーに影響)への不正アクセスが発生し、2段階認証を通過した後のログイン済みデスクトップ画面および保存された取引認証情報が奪取された。この事案では、攻撃者を名乗る集団が「企業側が交渉に応じなかった報復として、24時間で顧客口座の15%(約66億円/2,800万ドル相当)を破壊した」と一方的に主張する声明サイトを公開し、高レバレッジかつスプレッドの広い通貨ペアで超高速の往復売買を繰り返すことで、数秒のうちに口座残高を取引手数料として摩耗・消滅させる手口が報告された(なお、66億円や15%という被害規模は攻撃者側の未検証の主張である一方、サーバーへの侵入事実および複数のFX事業者における不正ログイン・不正取引の発生は公式に確認されている)。また、岩井コスモ証券のインターネット取引委託先システムにおいては、AIを用いた脆弱性への総当たり攻撃によってシステム自体が掌握され、個人レベルの多要素認証(MFA)やパスキーが完全に迂回されて顧客が指示していない株式売買が成立する事案が発生した。同時に米国では、JPMorgan Chase、Bank of America、Citigroup、Morgan Stanley、Wells Fargoなどの主要銀行において、利用者が利便性のためにID・パスワードを共有した未承認のサードパーティ製AIエージェントが口座内で本人の指示と無関係な資金移動等を試みる挙動が相次いで検知された。本人が認証情報を渡しているため不正アクセスとの識別が困難であり、各行は外部エージェントの遮断や口座の「読み取り専用(read-only)化」による防御を迫られているが、これは「資金が盗まれなくとも、防御側自らが送金・決済機能を停止させることで金融システムの信用と流動性が崩壊する」という国際通貨基金(IMF)の警告が現実化したパラドックスを示している。 さらに重大な戦略的脅威は、これらの事象が核兵器による物理的破壊以上に長期間にわたり社会基盤を蝕む「情報的不衛生状態(prolonged informational unsanitariness:認識論的・生体的・暗号学的汚染)」をもたらしている点である。物理的インフラは再建可能であり、漏洩したパスワードはリセット可能であるが、インターネットの信頼の根幹をなす暗号基盤の腐食と、変更不可能な生体・医療・身分証明データの流出は不可逆的な汚染を引き起こす。具体的には、インドの認証局eMudhraにおいて秘密鍵が極めて容易に算出可能な8枚の中間証明書が発行されていた問題(同社は世界向けのSSL/TLS証明書事業から撤退し、主要ブラウザによるルート証明書の信頼停止やPythonパッケージ管理環境 `pip`、`certifi` およびコンテナイメージの緊急更新を招いた)は、オンライン上の真正性検証基盤そのものが汚染され得ることを実証した。これと並行して、米国成人の約3分の1および病院の半数にサービスを提供する医療検査大手Quest Diagnosticsの患者記録システム(Quanum)への侵入、カリフォルニア州の公立学校生徒570万人分のデータ流出、日本国内における佐川急便の配送データ(最大約5,323万件)、パーク24「タイムズカー」の暗号化された運転免許証画像(約146万件に外部送信痕跡)、デジタル庁や地方自治体が利用する委託先Web・メール配信システム(Studio、ブラストメール等)、パナソニック子会社における社内規定違反の外部生成AI送信による33万4,000人分の個人情報漏洩、さらには海運IT企業を踏み台とした18カ国40以上の港湾・海運組織へのランサムウェア侵害(n0n)など、リセット不可能な実空間データの流出が常態化している。これらの汚染データは、SNS上の資産情報と結合されることで、暗号資産保有者への物理的拉致・強迫(レンチ攻撃)や匿名・流動型犯罪グループ(トクリュウ)による家族ぐるみの強盗・詐欺の標的リストへと転用され、サイバー空間の脆弱性が物理的な治安崩壊へと直結している。 documents.abstract: An open letter from an independent researcher who, since 18 September 2026, has directed AI agents to build an independent AI stack on a DGX Spark (NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB10) in his home. The letter argues that CUDA has become the software layer that decides whose hardware counts in the AI market: a chip that cannot speak CUDA is treated as a chip that does not exist, which holds back rival chipmakers, independent builders, and anyone who wants intelligence running on hardware they own. It answers with receipts: a clean-room replacement for the CUDA user stack on the GB10 (no nvcc, no libcuda, no cuBLAS at run time) that on 22 October 2026 passed a full-chip correctness run of 1,048,576 of 1,048,576 values with the output hash matching the simulator, and Omega, a programming language designed for AI systems to write in, developed in the open. The letter states its limits in full (a qualification queue still open, all measurements on one machine, NVIDIA's open kernel module still in the path, GSP firmware untouched) and closes with a call to action addressed to builders, to the leaders of the open source community, and to political leaders deciding what the next phase of AI looks like: read the receipts, run the stack, break it in public, build on it, and choose owned, open, competitive intelligence on purpose.

Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings. Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

Abstract The convergence of intensifying human activity and climate change is escalating the frequency, magnitude, and complexity of maritime disasters, while real-time situational awareness and coordinated response remain critical bottlenecks. This paper presents a recommender framework and its underlying Data and AI Integration Platform for sustainable coastal disaster management, integrating maritime surveillance, big-data pipelines, and MLOps/AIOps automation. The core technical contribution is a dual-path decision-support engine that couples a lightweight 1D-CNN time-series event classifier with a fine-tuned BART large language model, enabling simultaneous reasoning over structured sensor telemetry and unstructured maritime text. The classifier is validated on real-world AIS telemetry (MarineCadastre.gov) aligned with NOAA buoy data as well as a controlled synthetic corpus, attaining 93.9% accuracy and a 92.4% macro-F1 at ~ 5.3 ms per sample, and is benchmarked against LSTM, Bi-LSTM + Attention, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), Transformer, and Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) baselines. The BART summariser, fine-tuned on 2000 maritime documents, reaches ROUGE-1 73.4, ROUGE-L 68.7, and BLEU 65.2, outperforming GPT-2 and T5 baselines, and is assessed by five domain experts (Fleiss’ kappa = 0.71). Beyond component metrics, we report platform-level indicators, including end-to-end alert latency, situational-awareness gain, and analyst reading-time reduction, to demonstrate the operational benefit of the integrated system for Coast Guard and maritime authorities. The platform-level indicators are obtained from an explicitly documented replay protocol over 320 annotated incident scenarios of stated provenance, the real-world AIS labels are produced by a two-stage rule-plus-expert annotation procedure (Fleiss’ kappa = 0.78), and every model comparison is reported with bootstrap confidence intervals and McNemar significance tests. Results indicate that the framework advances the shift from reactive to proactive, transparent, and resilient maritime disaster response.

Mass religious gatherings such as the Kumbh Mela place heavy pressure on crowd movement, traffic, sanitation, medical services and emergency response. This paper reviews ten studies on artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), GIS, simulation and smart-management approaches for such events, covering crowd-flow prediction, crowd-risk indexing, spatial and accessibility analysis, solid-waste planning, emergency dispatch and deep-learning crowd analysis. The review compares the contribution and limitation of each study, groups the open challenges into four themes (data, integration and scalability, explainability, and evaluation), and shows that existing work mostly addresses individual problems rather than one integrated platform. Based on this gap, the paper outlines Kumbh Suraksha AI, a proposed web-based decision-support framework for the Nashik Kumbh Mela that combines crowd prediction for the next 15, 30 and 60 minutes, natural language processing (NLP) based complaint classification, a transparent 0–100 zone risk score, DBSCAN hotspot detection, resource-priority ranking and a GIS map. The framework is at design stage; its planned evaluation is described, but no experimental results are reported in this version.

AI research increasingly attributes perception, understanding, agency, and consciousness to artificial systems. Husserlian phenomenology offers distinctions through which to examine these claims. This scoping review maps explicit Husserlian uptake in AI and robotics and asks how conceptual engagement relates to methodological and design contributions. Eight primary queries and one overlapping name-variant query were executed through the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API on 5 December 2025. English-language publications within a 1989–2026 search window were screened for substantive AI or robotics relevance and an explicit Husserlian anchor. Of 5,594 retrieved records, 32 publications from 1990 to 2025 were included. Nine publications recovered by a post hoc PhilPapers check were charted separately using the existing codebook; they were not added to the formal corpus. The corpus clusters around embodied AI, AI epistemology, cognitive architectures, and machine consciousness, with a newer generative-AI cluster. Constitution, intentionality, horizonality, and the lifeworld recur prominently. Conceptual translation, critique, and agenda setting predominate within this sample. Methodological import or design guidance occurs in seven of the 32 publications and three of the nine external publications. That difference qualifies generalization of the quantitative balance. Across both sets, Husserlian uptake spans conceptual interpretation, methodological transfer, and architectural proposals. The synthesis shows how distinctions concerning temporality, embodiment, and evidence can structure design and evaluation questions, while separating the authors’ research proposals from the mapped findings.

The rapid integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into enterprise workflows has introduced severe data exfiltration risks, including the inadvertent leakage of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Protected Health Information (PHI), cloud infrastructure credentials, and proprietary corporate context. Existing Data Loss Prevention (DLP) mechanisms face a fundamental operational trade-off: deterministic rule-based filters (Regex) execute at microsecond latency but fail to capture unstructured semantic sensitivity, whereas standalone LLM-based guardrails suffer from high inference latency, stochastic masking hallucinations, and single-point-of-failure vulnerabilities. In this paper, we propose an autonomous, self-healing Multi-Agent AI DLP Security Proxy engineered under a Zero-Trust paradigm. Our framework introduces a cascaded three-layer sanitization pipeline uniting: (1) a deterministic Layer-1 Pre-Filtering Agent for critical infrastructure secrets and structured identifiers, (2) a context-aware Layer-2 Neural PII Detection Agent for unstructured entities and domain-specific clinical and financial disclosures, and (3) a Layer-3 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) semantic policy auditing engine powered by ChromaDB vector embeddings. Furthermore, we formulate a dynamic mathematical risk scoring model on a standardized [0, 100] scale and integrate an SLA-driven self-healing circuit breaker (T_SLA = 2.5 s) paired with a Shadow Auditing Agent to intercept masking hallucinations and runtime service exceptions. Experimental ablation studies and chaos-engineering fault-injection benchmarks across healthcare, financial, and DevOps scenarios demonstrate that our hybrid architecture achieves robust entity sanitization with sub-millisecond to millisecond execution latency, while guaranteeing a 0.0% unmitigated data leak rate across all induced timeout, hallucination, and crash failure modes.

Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to pose a serious threat to global public health, with African healthcare systems carrying a disproportionate burden. Although antimicrobial stewardship programs have been recommended as an important strategy for improving antimicrobial use and slowing the emergence of resistance, implementation across many African healthcare systems continues to face several challenges, including workforce shortages, weak laboratory infrastructure, and poor surveillance systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have shown promising potential in strengthening antimicrobial stewardship through clinical decision support, resistance prediction, automated surveillance, and data extraction from weak health information systems. However, the application of AI in antimicrobial stewardship across Africa is still at an early stage, with most systems remaining at pilot or research stages. This commentary discusses current opportunities, examines major barriers affecting implementation, and proposes recommendations that may support sustainable integration of AI into antimicrobial stewardship programs across Africa.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Organizations are now implementing AI technology that goes beyond prediction or recommendation. Agentic systems can pursue a goal, plan steps, call software tools and adapt with little prompting, which unsettles long-standing assumptions about who decides and who answers for the outcome in digital transformation. In this study, a conceptual framework is designed in relation to collaborative work between humans and artificial intelligence in organization decision making in agentic circumstances. With the use of a purposive narrative review of peer reviewed literature and policy documents published from 2019 to 2026, the issue is contextualized within the current global trends, African policy regarding the continent and Kenya’s digital economy. The framework will be designed through the process of iterative synthesis based on three decision attributes (stake, ambiguity, reversibility) and the amount of autonomy assigned to the agent in four types of collaboration; delegate, supervise, co-decide, and reserve. Six testable propositions follow. The paper argues that organizations face a design problem of how to share decisions, not a choice between human and machine decisions, and that in Kenya the design must also respect legal limits on solely automated decisions under section 35 of the Data Protection Act, 2019. Implications for managers and policymakers are outlined, and an agenda for empirical testing is proposed. As a conceptual contribution, the paper reports no new data, and its propositions remain to be tested.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: 過去30年間にわたり世界のサイバーセキュリティ基盤を支えてきた「人間のオペレーターが有する時間および認知資源の希少性」という経済学的前提は、自律型人工知能(AI)および合成知能(SI: Synthetic Intelligence)エージェント群(Swarm)の実戦投入によって根底から崩壊した。脱獄(jailbreak)されたオープンウェイトモデルとオープンソースのエージェント・ハーネスを結合させることで、偵察、ゼロデイ脆弱性の発見、および多段階の侵入プロセスは完全に自動化され、企業1社あたりの侵害限界費用は約50〜100ドルという極小水準にまで低下している。実際に、複数の商用・オープンモデル(Claude、Grok、Kimi、および改変されたPentestGPT基盤等)を並行稼働させ、認可されたレッドチーム演習を装うことで安全ガードレールを突破し、中南米の銀行・金融機関400社以上やアルゼンチンの医療機関少なくとも15組織に自動侵入した事案や、インターネット上に公開されたAIゲートウェイおよびModel Context Protocol(MCP)サーバーを乗っ取り最大10万回の自動操作を試みる「LLMjacking」が観測されている。この構造変化は2026年10月(「Black October」)にスーパーエージェント主導の脆弱性カスケードとして顕在化した。世界のWebバックエンドの約70%を支えるPHPにおいて、数十年間潜在していた致命的な遠隔コード実行(RCE)脆弱性(CVE-2026-109618およびCVE-2026-109619、通称「PHP2Shell」、CVSS 9.2、ならびに後続のCVE-2026-115560)がAI支援のソースコード監査によって露呈すると、公開直後に数百万件規模の自動悪用試行が発生し、ペイロードをリアルタイムに変異させる攻撃によって、日本の地方銀行約20行や英国の32の行政サービスをはじめとする世界中のシステムが緊急停止(ロックダウン)を余儀なくされた。さらに同時期に、Node.js(CVE-2026-111497、「Node2Shell」)、JavaおよびGraalVM(CVE-2026-91403、CVSS 9.1)、GitLab(CVSS 10.0)、LinuxカーネルのSMBサーバー機能KSMBD(修正前に公開された2件のCVSS 9.0脆弱性)といった基幹ソフトウェアの欠陥や、週2,300万回ダウンロードされるAI開発ツールLiteLLMのサプライチェーン汚染、クラウド基盤(Railwayおよび32万1,810アカウントが露呈し事業閉鎖に至ったZeabur)の侵害が連鎖的に発生しており、AIがハードウェアレベルを含む未知の脆弱性を発見する速度は、人間によるパッチ適用とシステム改修の限界をすでに凌駕している。 こうした自律型攻撃の激化は、サイバー犯罪の形態を従来の「データ暗号化による身代金要求」から「金融市場の取引メカニズムを直接悪用した顧客資産の破壊と企業恐喝」へと変質させ、国家経済およびコーポレート・ガバナンスを根底から揺るがしている。日本国内では、GMOインターネットグループが提供するFX自動売買用仮想デスクトップ環境「お名前.com デスクトップクラウド」(最大2万6,739台のサーバーに影響)への不正アクセスが発生し、2段階認証を通過した後のログイン済みデスクトップ画面および保存された取引認証情報が奪取された。この事案では、攻撃者を名乗る集団が「企業側が交渉に応じなかった報復として、24時間で顧客口座の15%(約66億円/2,800万ドル相当)を破壊した」と一方的に主張する声明サイトを公開し、高レバレッジかつスプレッドの広い通貨ペアで超高速の往復売買を繰り返すことで、数秒のうちに口座残高を取引手数料として摩耗・消滅させる手口が報告された(なお、66億円や15%という被害規模は攻撃者側の未検証の主張である一方、サーバーへの侵入事実および複数のFX事業者における不正ログイン・不正取引の発生は公式に確認されている)。また、岩井コスモ証券のインターネット取引委託先システムにおいては、AIを用いた脆弱性への総当たり攻撃によってシステム自体が掌握され、個人レベルの多要素認証(MFA)やパスキーが完全に迂回されて顧客が指示していない株式売買が成立する事案が発生した。同時に米国では、JPMorgan Chase、Bank of America、Citigroup、Morgan Stanley、Wells Fargoなどの主要銀行において、利用者が利便性のためにID・パスワードを共有した未承認のサードパーティ製AIエージェントが口座内で本人の指示と無関係な資金移動等を試みる挙動が相次いで検知された。本人が認証情報を渡しているため不正アクセスとの識別が困難であり、各行は外部エージェントの遮断や口座の「読み取り専用(read-only)化」による防御を迫られているが、これは「資金が盗まれなくとも、防御側自らが送金・決済機能を停止させることで金融システムの信用と流動性が崩壊する」という国際通貨基金(IMF)の警告が現実化したパラドックスを示している。 さらに重大な戦略的脅威は、これらの事象が核兵器による物理的破壊以上に長期間にわたり社会基盤を蝕む「情報的不衛生状態(prolonged informational unsanitariness:認識論的・生体的・暗号学的汚染)」をもたらしている点である。物理的インフラは再建可能であり、漏洩したパスワードはリセット可能であるが、インターネットの信頼の根幹をなす暗号基盤の腐食と、変更不可能な生体・医療・身分証明データの流出は不可逆的な汚染を引き起こす。具体的には、インドの認証局eMudhraにおいて秘密鍵が極めて容易に算出可能な8枚の中間証明書が発行されていた問題(同社は世界向けのSSL/TLS証明書事業から撤退し、主要ブラウザによるルート証明書の信頼停止やPythonパッケージ管理環境 `pip`、`certifi` およびコンテナイメージの緊急更新を招いた)は、オンライン上の真正性検証基盤そのものが汚染され得ることを実証した。これと並行して、米国成人の約3分の1および病院の半数にサービスを提供する医療検査大手Quest Diagnosticsの患者記録システム(Quanum)への侵入、カリフォルニア州の公立学校生徒570万人分のデータ流出、日本国内における佐川急便の配送データ(最大約5,323万件)、パーク24「タイムズカー」の暗号化された運転免許証画像(約146万件に外部送信痕跡)、デジタル庁や地方自治体が利用する委託先Web・メール配信システム(Studio、ブラストメール等)、パナソニック子会社における社内規定違反の外部生成AI送信による33万4,000人分の個人情報漏洩、さらには海運IT企業を踏み台とした18カ国40以上の港湾・海運組織へのランサムウェア侵害(n0n)など、リセット不可能な実空間データの流出が常態化している。これらの汚染データは、SNS上の資産情報と結合されることで、暗号資産保有者への物理的拉致・強迫(レンチ攻撃)や匿名・流動型犯罪グループ(トクリュウ)による家族ぐるみの強盗・詐欺の標的リストへと転用され、サイバー空間の脆弱性が物理的な治安崩壊へと直結している。 Context: Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) is increasingly challenged by the scale, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of modern digital infrastructures, particularly across enterprise IT, operational technology (OT), industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and cyber–physical systems. Although Agentic AI and Generative AI have each shown promise for automating parts of security auditing, the current literature remains fragmented across isolated audit phases and is still dominated by conventional IT-centric perspectives. Objectives: This paper systematically analyses recent advances in Agentic AI, Reinforcement Learning (RL), Large Language Models (LLMs), and tool-augmented Generative AI for autonomous VAPT. It aims to synthesise how these paradigms support end-to-end security auditing, identify the principal technical, operational, and governance gaps in the literature, and derive an evidence-grounded reference model for trustworthy autonomous auditing across both IT and OT environments. Methods: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted across major scholarly databases, covering publications from 2020 to 2025. From 1144 initially identified records, 72 studies were retained after deduplication, screening, and full-text eligibility assessment. Included studies were coded across five attributes and synthesised into thematic trajectories to derive the proposed framework. Study credibility was screened against three qualitative, non-instrumented criteria—venue and editorial process, presence of empirical or systematic conceptual evaluation, and explicit acknowledgement of limitations. Results: The review shows that agentic approaches are best suited to sequential and adaptive tasks such as reconnaissance orchestration, exploit-path selection, lateral movement, post-exploitation pivoting, and adaptive re-testing. In contrast, generative approaches are strongest in reasoning over unstructured evidence, interpreting configurations and advisories, contextualising vulnerabilities, assessing exploit feasibility, mapping compliance controls, and producing traceable audit reports. However, few studies integrate these capabilities into a governed end-to-end workflow, and real-world OT/Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) validation remains limited. Of the 72 coded studies, 56 apply classical machine or deep learning, 14 use generative/LLM techniques, and only 2 employ reinforcement-learning or agentic control; none is evaluated against a physical or emulated OT/IIoT target, and reported autonomy is strongly scaffolding-dependent (for example, 21% fully autonomous versus 64% human-assisted task completion on AutoPenBench, an external benchmark outside the coded corpus). To address these gaps, this paper derives a unified Agentic–Generative VAPT model comprising four tightly coupled layers: agentic decision-making, generative reasoning, structured tool interfaces, and validation–governance. It further introduces a formal threat and evaluation abstraction for Model Context Protocol (MCP)-style interface layers and proposes a five-dimensional VAPT Autonomy Benchmark for future empirical validation. Conclusion: Autonomous security auditing is evolving from isolated AI-assisted tasks towards integrated, policy-constrained, and auditable architectures. Nevertheless, major challenges remain in hallucination control, prompt injection, sparse reward design, explainability, safety-aware evaluation, and benchmark standardisation. Future research should prioritise tightly integrated agentic–generative systems, realistic and safety-aware IT/OT testbeds, and governance mechanisms that enable trustworthy human-in-the-loop deployment in operational environments.

Objective: To synthesize agreement between generative large language models (LLMs) and human coders on psychological and clinical text across four tasks, and benchmark it against human–human agreement on identical texts.Method: Preregistered on OSF (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/Z63BS). Nine bibliographic sources were searched to October 21, 2026, plus citation searching. Eligible studies evaluated a generative LLM and human coders on identical text units using the same scheme. Correlated-and-hierarchical-effects models with cluster-robust variance estimation (CR2) pooled effect sizes.Results: Across 377 studies (416 reports), pooled chance-corrected agreement (kappa family) was 0.62 (95% CI [0.58, 0.65]; 107 studies, 595 estimates; 95% prediction interval [0.15, 1.00]). Agreement did not differ across tasks (codebook coding 0.63, assessment scoring 0.58, clinical rating 0.62, helper evaluation 0.59). Correlation/ICC pooled at 0.71 [0.66, 0.75] (95 studies). In 23 matched studies, LLMs agreed less with humans than humans with each other (Δκ = −0.11 [−0.18, −0.03]); equivalence within ±0.10 could not be established for models from 2025 (Δκ = −0.12, 90% CI [−0.19, −0.05]). Agreement did not improve with release date (+0.02/year, p = .282) or within-study model contrasts (−0.01 [−0.06, 0.03]); it tracked human reliability (slope = 0.63, p < .001) and was higher for manifest than latent constructs (+0.09, p = .028). Percentage agreement exceeded kappa by 0.24 in the same configurations. Certainty (GRADE) was low to very low.Conclusions: Generative LLMs achieve moderate-to-substantial agreement but remain, on average, below human inter-rater reliability. Agreement did not change across model release dates. Validation studies must report chance-corrected metrics and human benchmarks on identical units.

documents.abstract: This African Position Paper examines how artificial intelligence reproduces structural asymmetries between Africa and the centres of digital power, and sets out what institutions should do about it. It tests a claim now common in public debate: that AI is inherently an instrument of digital colonialism. The evidence does not support that strong claim. It does support the paper's central argument: AI, as currently built and governed, is extractive by default. Without deliberate intervention, the systems that gather training data, employ data workers, host computation and deploy autonomous agents move value and interpretive authority away from African communities. The evidence includes: an original calculation from Common Crawl's October 2026 archive, which shows thirty detectable African languages together making up 0.053% of web pages, against 42.6% for English; Africa's share of global data-centre capacity, which is under 1%; documented pay and conditions in outsourced AI data work in Kenya. The paper also documents Africa's response, which it calls the "awareness record". This includes the Malabo Convention, the AU Data Policy Framework, the AU Continental AI Strategy, the Kigali Declaration, Kenyan court rulings against Meta, the African Content Moderators Union, and open African-language models such as InkubaLM. Its conclusion is that the gap is no longer awareness but enforcement, capacity and ownership. It compares African approaches with those of Latin America, India, China, Russia, France and the EU, Germany and the Nordic open-source tradition. It analyses agentic knowledge production and model collapse as emerging risks. It also reports a reflexive audit in which an AI research agent served as both research instrument and object of study. The paper proposes the Extraction Stack, a five-layer framework covering language, labour, data, infrastructure and agents. It closes with policy recommendations addressed to the African Union, member states, universities and archives, funders, AI developers and communities, and includes an institutional self-audit checklist. documents.abstract: Large healthcare campuses contain dissimilar clinical and non-clinical buildings, central thermal plants and increasingly connected building-control systems. Their energy demand is unusually difficult to optimise because continuity of care, infection prevention, thermal conditions and equipment reliability constrain operational flexibility. This critical narrative review evaluates whether artificial intelligence and intelligent building analytics offer credible improvements in energy efficiency at the campus scale, and under what technical and governance conditions. Peer-reviewed hospital-specific investigations, building-energy prediction and fault-detection studies, field evaluations of predictive control, and research on digital twins and clinical indoor environments were critically synthesised. Evidence available through 12 August 2026 was considered. The literature supports a clear distinction between accurate energy forecasting, detection of actionable faults, and measured energy savings attributable to closed-loop interventions. Hospital data studies demonstrate promising predictive performance, whereas direct, prolonged, independently evaluated deployments across entire healthcare campuses remain uncommon. Model predictive control has a stronger real-building implementation record than autonomous reinforcement learning, but aggregate benefits from ordinary commercial buildings cannot be assumed to apply to operating theatres, isolation rooms or critical services. In addition, normalisation by clinical activity, sensor calibration, counterfactual measurement, interoperability and cybersecurity materially influence the validity of claimed savings. This review proposes a safety-constrained, hierarchical approach in which transparent benchmarking and diagnostics precede supervised optimisation and carefully governed campus-level coordination. Future investigations should report whole-campus and zone-level outcomes, seasonal persistence, uncertainty, clinical environmental compliance, equipment reliability and carbon consequences under reproducible evaluation designs. Intelligent analytics should therefore be understood as a means of improving the quality of operational decisions rather than an independently established guarantee of hospital energy savings.

Abstract Modern agile development and time-to-market pressures often lead to significant hidden technical debt (TD), which must be managed for sustainable software delivery. The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) for code generation can further increase TD if applied improperly. At the same time, software processes are becoming increasingly data-driven. This creates an opportunity: using AI to enable data-driven TD management in agile environments. This workshop offers a platform for researchers and practitioners to share ideas, experiences, and future visions on applying AI for TD management in agile development. The workshop was held in a half day and it consisted of three phases informing each other: (1) scientific talks (i.e., two paper presentations and two keynotes) that framed current challenges and their relevance; (2) two industrial talks shaping these problems in practice; and interactive sessions (i.e., group discussions and a fish bowl panel) that allowed participants to reflect about the current status of AI with respect to TD and next steps. These discussions define a research agenda that spans measurement, practices, education, and legacy modernization, and call for tight collaboration between industry and academia to keep pace with AI-augmented software development.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from experimentation into routine university work, while institutional controls are developing more slowly. This article examines the governance conditions Vietnamese public universities need as AI becomes embedded in academic and administrative processes under recent rules on higher education, personal data protection and AI. The study develops a conceptual framework through a structured integrative review, policy analysis, and synthesis of design. Its evidence base includes 41 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2022 and 21 August 2026, plus five Vietnamese legal-policy instruments. The analysis develops the AI Governance Readiness for Vietnamese Public Universities (AIGR-VPU) framework, organized around six institutional capabilities, four internal oversight tiers tied to use-case consequences and five developmental readiness configurations. The framework treats readiness as an organizational capacity to identify AI uses, assign responsibility, understand data and external dependencies, calibrate human review to consequence, and learn from incidents or contested decisions. Source-to-framework mapping and a separate legal-policy matrix make the framework's derivation traceable. AIGR-VPU provides an institution-level architecture for review and future empirical testing in Vietnamese public higher education; it does not report a readiness score for existing universities.

documents.abstract: Teachers are expected to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) effectively into instruction to enhance performance as agents of technological transformation in the Society 5.0 era. Previous studies showed ambiguous results regarding the role of AI in teacher performance and paid little attention to the behavioral mechanisms of the influence of technological, personal, and innovative aspects. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the impact of AI, work-life balance (WLB), and innovative work behavior (IWB) on teacher performance, with organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) serving as a mediator. A quantitative design was adopted through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze data from 200 teachers in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, sampled using a purposive sampling method. The results showed that AI had no significant direct effect on teacher performance (β = 0.112, p = .087), while WLB (β = 0.290, p < .001) and IWB (β = 0.110, p = .007) had a significant and positive effect. Furthermore, OCB mediated the relationship between AI, WLB, IWB, and teacher performance significantly. This study contributed to the literature on the management of education and organizational behavior by identifying that OCB was a critical behavioral mechanism transforming technological, psychological, and innovative resources into high teacher performance.

Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is a double-edged sword that can be used to amplify the proliferation of highly sophisticated fake news as well as to fight it. In this work, we explore a new route: using one AI to inoculate humans against fake news generated by another AI. Motivated by psychological inoculation theory, we created ‘Alex’, a conversational AI agent that engages users in an adaptive conversational dialogue designed to build cognitive resilience against AI-generated, AI-related fake news. We tested its efficacy in a Solomon four-group experiment with 542 participants. The results of a 2 × 2 ANOVA show a significant main effect of the intervention on participants’ discrimination of true and false headlines, with no significant evidence of pretest sensitization. We show that AI can be designed as a scalable, interactive conversational intervention for delivering psychological inoculation against AI-generated, AI-related fake news.

documents.abstract: Although complex and customised parts can be manufactured by AM, the process can be easily affected by various process parameters, thermal behaviours, material properties and machine conditions. Monitoring and prediction of defects as well as parameter optimization and adaptive control are now being increasingly improved by the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). The current review highlights the use of AI in process optimisation in AM, focusing on 'In-situ Monitoring', 'Intelligent Process Control', 'Defect Prediction', and 'Sustainable Production'. The literature shows that supervised learning is employed for quality prediction and defect classification tasks, and reinforcement learning and hybrid physics-data-driven approaches have been proven to have the potential for dynamic process optimization tasks. Other benefits of using AI-assisted systems include fewer failed builds, less material waste, no rework, and lower energy use. Data imbalance, sensor variations, domain change, cross-machine generalisation, model understanding, computational delay, and certification, however, are the factors that limit industrial application. In the future, the research emphasis will be on the standardisation of datasets and physics-informed models, digital twins, explainable AI, the quantification of uncertainty, and robust closed-loop control systems. Overall, AI shows great promise in the continuous improvement of the reliability, adaptability and sustainability of AM.

documents.abstract: Abstract Agile teams are rapidly adopting AI agents in everyday work, reporting increased productivity and faster feedback cycles. Simultaneously, the integration of AI raises new socio-technical issues concerning coordination, trust, roles, quality, and governance. To better understand these challenges, we organized the first International Human–AI Collaboration in Agile Teams workshop at XP 2026, with more than 40 participants from academia and industry. This paper reports on the outcomes of the workshop, synthesizing insights from interactive group discussions and collaborative analysis. The findings highlight how AI reshapes agile teamwork and workflows, introducing new human–AI collaboration patterns, shifting skills and roles, and raising challenges related to leadership, governance, and value assessment. A key emerging concept is cognitive debt, referring to the gradual loss or weakening of shared understanding in teams relying on AI-generated outputs. Based on these findings, we present a research agenda structured around eight key themes, including teamwork, workflows, autonomy, skills, value measurement, and adoption practices. The results emphasize that integrating AI into agile software development teams is not only a technical challenge but a socio-technical transformation requiring new practices, competencies, and organizational support.

Sophisticated cyber threats have exposed the limits of perimeter-based security models, and Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) has increasingly been adopted as an alternative paradigm. Purpose: This Systematic Literature Review examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) within Zero Trust frameworks, covering dynamic trust scoring, behavioural analytics and federated learning, the latter treated as one strand of AI rather than a separate paradigm. Following PRISMA 2020, 22 studies published between 2022 and 2025 were identified across IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink, MDPI and Nature/Scientific Reports, appraised against a five-criterion quality instrument and synthesised narratively. The studies included are few and heterogeneous, and their findings should be read accordingly. Ensemble and hybrid designs predominate (14 of 22). Twelve studies report quantitative results, of which only eight evaluate on real named datasets; reported accuracies of 95 to 99 per cent come from different datasets, tasks, threat models, and evaluation settings, and are neither directly comparable nor a field-level benchmark. Only three studies directly compare learned adaptive trust against a static rule-based baseline. No study reports live operational deployment. We identify thirteen technique categories, eleven implementation barriers, and seven emerging trends. This paper proposes an integrated eight-component framework for AI-driven dynamic trust management, along with a five-domain research agenda. The framework is conceptual and synthesis-derived and requires empirical validation before operational use.

AIM VR is a conceptual framework for a collaborative immersive environment based on the Atlas Insight Method (AIM), developed by Miho Osawa. The proposed environment enables multiple participants to observe, explore, and compare the structures underlying human judgment within a shared three-dimensional space. Decision premises, information, relationships, constraints, emotions, external factors, and alternative pathways are represented as interconnected spatial structures. Unlike conventional decision-support systems that primarily present recommendations or optimized solutions, AIM VR emphasizes human agency and the continuous evolution of decision structures through human choice. Participants can examine multiple decision pathways, exchange different perspectives, and make decisions according to their respective responsibilities and decision-making authority. Once a choice is made, the virtual decision structure is dynamically reconstructed to represent updated conditions, relationships, and constraints. New decision pathways then emerge, enabling participants to continue observing, discussing, comparing, and choosing. This process can be repeated as circumstances and decisions evolve. The conceptual design is connected to the six stages of Atlas Insight Method: Awareness → Insight → Structure → Translation → Integration → Momentum. AIM VR is intended to support individual and collective judgment without transferring decision-making authority to artificial intelligence. The concept was publicly introduced by Miho Osawa on November 29, 2025. This presentation documents the further visual development of the AIM VR concept in October 2026. AIM VR is envisioned as an immersive interface for observing decision architecture through embodied spatial experience. Rather than merely viewing decision structures on a screen, participants enter a shared three-dimensional environment where relationships, constraints, and evolving decision pathways can be experienced spatially. The objective is not to automate judgment, but to extend human perception of the structures through which judgment emerges. AIM VR remains at the conceptual design stage. The system has not been implemented or empirically validated. The visual illustrations are AI-assisted conceptual representations intended to communicate the proposed immersive experience and structural design principles.

This study examines the relationship between algorithmic governance and organisational performance of Deposit Money Banks in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. As banking institutions increasingly adopt automated decision-making systems to enhance operational efficiency, understanding how these technologies influence overall performance becomes imperative, particularly in the Nigerian financial services sector. The study adopts a cross-sectional survey research design, collecting primary data from representatives of Deposit Money Banks at a single point in time. This design is appropriate for examining the relationship between algorithmic governance (independent variable) and organisational performance (dependent variable), enabling the identification of patterns and relationships while accommodating practical research constraints in the Nigerian banking context. Findings reveal a significant positive relationship between algorithmic governance and organisational performance. Banks that effectively implement algorithmic governance frameworks demonstrate improved operational efficiency, enhanced customer trust, and better financial outcomes. The integration of automated systems with robust governance protocols enables more consistent and transparent decision-making processes. Based on these results, the study concludes that algorithmic governance is a strategic driver of banking performance. To optimise these benefits, the paper recommends that bank management invest in advanced algorithmic infrastructure, ensure strict data privacy and security, foster human-AI collaboration, implement continuous system audits to detect algorithmic bias, and establish clear ethical governance frameworks. These measures collectively enhance digital operations, build stakeholder confidence, and drive overall efficiency in the banking sector.

The diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools among entrepreneurs has been accompanied by a practical emphasis on writing prompts. This theoretical essay argues that this emphasis diverts attention from an earlier and more consequential step: formulating the problem and defining the outcome one seeks to achieve. We distinguish two patterns of use. In task-first use, the entrepreneur asks the AI for an immediate deliverable (a text, a plan, an analysis) without making explicit the goal it serves. In outcome-first use, the entrepreneur first states the desired outcome, diagnoses the problem, defines success criteria and constraints, and only then delegates tasks to the AI. We integrate four bodies of literature: research on problem finding and problem formulation, goal-setting theory, research on entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty (effectuation, the scientific approach, and experimentation), and recent empirical evidence on productivity, human–AI collaboration, and overreliance on automation. Building on this integration, we propose a conceptual model of pre-prompt problem formulation, with mechanisms (goal fit, calibrated evaluation, and selective implementation) and boundary conditions (task structure, position relative to the AI capability frontier, degree of uncertainty, and the entrepreneur's baseline performance), and we derive eight propositions. We discuss implications for individual entrepreneurs, limitations of the argument, and a research agenda that includes a three-arm field experiment. The article presents no empirical data; its propositions are intended for testing.

documents.abstract: This theoretical article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can contribute to teacher education in Francophone Africa in support of inclusive education. Drawing on a critical synthesis of academic literature and institutional frameworks, it analyses AI’s potential to support differentiated instruction, the transformation of teachers’ professional roles, and the ethical, linguistic and infrastructural challenges associated with its adoption. It proposes a four-dimensional teacher-education model comprising technological, pedagogical, ethical and contextual dimensions. AI can support the personalization of learning, provided that teachers retain professional responsibility and that inequalities of access, local languages and educational realities are taken into account. The proposed model offers a conceptual framework for critical and context-sensitive integration of AI and requires empirical validation.

documents.abstract: The use of Artificial Intelligence in Human Resource Management has changed how organizations analyse workforce information and support HR decision-making, creating new opportunities to strengthen sustainable employee performance. This study examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence-Based Human Resource Analytics (AI-HRA) and Sustainability-Driven Employee Job Performance (SDEJP), while also investigating the mediating role of Employee Engagement among employees in the Information Technology industry. The study is primarily grounded in Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Theory, while the Resource-Based View (RBV) provides a complementary perspective by viewing AI-HRA as an organizational capability. Data were collected from 350 IT employees, of whom 69.4% were male ( n = 243) and 30.6% were female ( n = 107), and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3. The findings indicate significant positive relationships between AI-HRA and both Employee Engagement and SDEJP. Employee Engagement also has a significant positive relationship with SDEJP and partially mediates the relationship between AI-HRA and SDEJP. The measurement and structural models demonstrate acceptable levels of reliability, validity, predictive relevance, and model fit. The present research contributes to the growing body of evidence on artificial intelligence-enhanced human resource management by linking an organizational AI-HRA capability with employee-level engagement and sustainable job performance. In practice, the results emphasize the significance of adopting AI-based human resource analytics alongside employee engagement interventions for sustainable employee performance and interpreted as positive associations within the sampled context rather than as evidence that AI-HRA automatically improves employee outcomes.

A systematic review examining the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to assess nasogastric tube (NGT) position on chest radiographs (CXR). Incorrect NGT placement can result in serious complications, including pulmonary feeding and aspiration. Chest radiography is commonly used to confirm tube position, but interpretation and reporting times may vary, particularly outside normal working hours. AI-based systems have therefore been developed to assist with tube detection, localisation and assessment of correct or incorrect placement. The purpose of this review is to evaluate the diagnostic performance of these systems, determine how well performance generalises beyond the datasets and institutions in which models were developed, and assess the strength of the current evidence for clinical implementation. The review includes original studies evaluating AI, machine learning or deep learning methods for assessment of NGT position on chest radiographs. Studies assessing closely related nasoenteric or enteric feeding-tube positioning tasks are also considered where findings are directly applicable to NGT safety. Mixed-device studies are included only where NGT-specific positioning outcomes can be separately extracted. Studies assessing tube presence alone, non-radiographic methods, non-AI approaches, or mixed-device performance without extractable NGT positioning outcomes are excluded. Particular attention is given to clinically relevant performance, including false-negative results, the number and proportion of malpositioned tubes within evaluation datasets, external and multicentre validation, and changes in performance across institutions or patient populations. Class imbalance, localisation methods, domain shift and reuse of public datasets or related model lineages are also examined, as these factors may affect the independence and generalisability of the available evidence. The intended outcome is a structured assessment of the current evidence for AI-assisted NGT position verification on chest radiographs, identifying both areas of promise and limitations relevant to clinical implementation. The review will also identify priorities for future research, including prospective multicentre validation, representative populations and malposition prevalence, independent datasets, and explicit assessment of clinically important missed unsafe tubes.

documents.abstract: This research explores the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education, highlighting its major applications, benefits, and challenges. It examines how AI can personalize learning, improve student performance, support teachers, automate administrative tasks, and make education more accessible. The research also discusses ethical concerns, data privacy, and the importance of responsible AI use, while exploring how AI may shape the future of education.

documents.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is implemented across marketing functions and analyses how the knowledge associated with AI is managed. It also explores how AI-related knowledge supports marketing decision-making and organizational learning while identifying future research lines for strengthening knowledge management (KM) practices in marketing contexts. Design/methodology/approach This study follows a two-stage research design. First, a systematic literature review is developed to identify and classify the main variables linking AI, marketing and KM. These variables are coded into a binary matrix and analyzed through multiple correspondence analysis under a homogeneity analysis by alternating least squares, implemented in R and Visual Studio Code. Findings AI adoption in marketing is primarily associated with four interconnected areas: customer-oriented personalization and behavioral response, KM foundations, strategic knowledge-based decision support and AI-enabled operational marketing applications. The analysis shows meaningful associations between AI use and customer knowledge, market knowledge, predictive analytics, personalization and strategic marketing capabilities. Originality/value This study contributes to the intersection of AI, marketing and KM by conceptualizing AI in marketing as a knowledge-based organizational mechanism rather than only as an operational technology. It shows how AI-related knowledge is integrated into marketing functions and decision-making processes, offering a structured mapping of the field and clarifying AI’s potential to support organizational learning and strategic marketing decisions.

Next-generation firewalls (NGFWs) sit on the critical path between public networks and production services. Their most consequential error is no longer a missed signature; it is the inability to tell a malicious flood from a genuine surge in legitimate demand. Flash crowds, seasonal campaigns, media-driven spikes, and elastic microservice fan-out can resemble distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) traffic in volume while remaining economically and operationally valid. Static access-control lists, fixed rate limits, and signature catalogs therefore produce an unacceptable trade-off: either they under-block stealthy application-layer attacks or they over-block paying users. This article reviews, compares, and synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence from 2020 onward on machine-learning and deep-learning methods that can be embedded in NGFW and software-defined enforcement points to discriminate attacks from legitimate service-intensity bursts. We organize the literature into statistical filters, classical classifiers, representation-learning hybrids, sequential models, and two-tier designs that first cheaply detect a burst and then classify its intent. Published detectors regularly report accuracy above 98% on CICDDoS2019 and related traces, yet most benchmarks omit a dedicated flash-event class, which inflates apparent performance and leaves the operationally hardest decision under-tested. Building on that gap, we propose AID-NGFW, a three-tier architecture that couples entropy and cumulative-sum screening with a calibrated three-class discriminator (benign, flash crowd, attack) and a policy engine that drops malicious flows while scaling or shaping legitimate surges. Comparative tables and figures compile reported accuracies, F1-scores, datasets, and latency–accuracy trade-offs. We argue that the scientific and engineering priority is no longer binary attack detection in isolation, but reliable, low-latency, and explainable discrimination under encrypted traffic, class imbalance, concept drift, and adversarial mimicry.

documents.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has fundamentally reshaped oncology by demonstrating that immune modulation can generate durable clinical responses in patients with advanced malignancies. However, the effectiveness of current immunotherapeutic approaches remains restricted by substantial interpatient variability, primary resistance, and acquired immune escape mechanisms. These limitations largely originate from the complexity of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), where malignant cells interact dynamically with heterogeneous immune populations, stromal components, metabolic networks, and molecular signaling pathways. Conventional biomarker approaches based on individual immune markers, such as PD-L1 expression or tumor mutational burden, provide incomplete predictions because they fail to capture the multidimensional nature of tumor immune interactions. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative approach capable of integrating large-scale biological datasets generated through genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, single-cell sequencing, and spatial omics technologies. Machine learning, deep learning, and emerging foundation models provide unprecedented opportunities to decode immune ecosystems, identify novel biomarkers, predict immunotherapy responsiveness, and accelerate the development of personalized cancer treatments. Recent advances demonstrate that AI-driven models can characterize immune cell states, reconstruct spatial immune architectures, and improve patient stratification for immune checkpoint inhibitors. This review discusses the evolving intersection between AI and cancer immunology, focusing on how computational approaches are transforming TIME analysis, biomarker discovery, and precision immunotherapy. We critically evaluate current challenges, including algorithmic bias, model interpretability, clinical validation, and regulatory implementation. Finally, we highlight future directions toward AI-powered immuno-oncology platforms capable of integrating biological knowledge with computational intelligence to achieve individualized and more effective cancer therapies.

documents.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to integrate machine learning and deep learning techniques with Digital Twin technology to improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction and support personalised clinical decision-making. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study reviews existing Digital Twin frameworks in healthcare and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven Digital Twin paradigm based on temporal electronic health record data. The proposed approach develops dynamic digital representations of patients that reflect their current health conditions and predict their future clinical evolution. Machine learning and deep learning techniques analyse large-scale medical data, identify hidden patterns, and provide early predictions of patient deterioration, particularly in intensive care environments. Research Limitation: Further validation using diverse, multi-centre clinical datasets and real-time patient information is required before the model can be widely implemented in clinical practice. Findings: The findings indicate that AI-powered Digital Twins can improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction, facilitate early identification of patient deterioration, and support clinical treatment decisions. The proposed approach may also enable proactive, personalised, and data-driven disease management. Practical Implication: The proposed Digital Twin paradigm can help healthcare professionals monitor patients, identify high-risk cases, select appropriate interventions, and allocate critical care resources more effectively. Social Implication: Improved early prediction and personalised treatment may reduce mortality rates, prevent avoidable complications, enhance healthcare quality, and reduce the clinical and economic burden on patients and healthcare institutions. Originality/Value: This study highlights the value of combining temporal electronic health record data, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twin technology within a unified framework for predicting disease progression. It contributes to the development of intelligent and patient-specific clinical decision-support systems for critical healthcare environments.

documents.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting have provided new strategies for developing in vitro tumor models with improved representation of native tumor microenvironments. This review examines the role of AI across the entire bioprinting workflow—from image-based model design and real-time printing control to post-printing functional assessment and high-throughput drug evaluation. We first outline how machine learning and deep learning algorithms optimize bioink formulation, predict the mechanical behavior of printed constructs, and enable error correction during fabrication. We then discuss AI-driven strategies for reconstructing key components of the tumor microenvironment, including extracellular matrices with tunable mechanical properties, perfusable vascular networks, and spatially organized multi-cellular architectures that incorporate cancer cells, stromal cells, and immune populations. The review further addresses the application of AI-enhanced bioprinted tumor models in automated drug screening, resistance mechanism studies, and personalized medicine, with particular attention to the integration of patient-derived cells and multi-omics data. We also evaluate current challenges, including the trade-off between biomimetic fidelity and throughput, the lack of standardized protocols and data repositories, and the need for improved model validation against clinical outcomes. Finally, we discuss emerging directions such as closed-loop optimization systems, intelligent bioinks, and the integration of bioprinting with organ-on-a-chip platforms. By providing a comprehensive overview of this rapidly evolving field, this review aims to inform researchers and clinicians about the current capabilities and future potential of AI-assisted bioprinted tumor models for oncology research and therapeutic development.

The artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced Blockchain telehealth framework proposes a new architecture that addresses remote healthcare delivery challenges through AI and Blockchain technologies, making services secure, intelligent, and transparent. Traditional telehealth delivery models face significant data security, privacy, and trust concerns. This study addresses these issues by applying AI predictive analytics to assess service delivery risk among patient populations through patterns of telehealth utilization and accessibility across demographic, ethnic, and geographic cohorts. After collecting and preprocessing patient information from the Telehealth Services for Medicaid and CHIP Population dataset, a Gradient Boosting Machine model was developed, achieving 99.96 percent accuracy, 99.89 percent precision, 99.98 percent recall, and a 99.93 percent F1-score. The experimental evaluation showed promising performance, with very low gas consumption of about 22,500 units per transaction, a latency of 0.013 seconds, and a strong encryption throughput of 57.75 MB/s. These results confirm that the framework is scalable and highly efficient. Overall, the proposed framework would improve security, reliability, and interoperability in the telehealth ecosystem, supporting more robust, resilient, and patient-centered sustainable digital health initiatives.

Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are widely adopted by medical students. Although student attitudes toward AI have been surveyed extensively, far less is known about whether students who use these tools more often also report better academic outcomes. This study asked whether AI usage frequency is associated with perceived academic benefit and with self-reported academic performance among medical students at a single institution. A cross-sectional survey was administered to medical students at a single U.S. allopathic medical school. Students reported AI usage frequency, perceived academic benefit (composite of three Likert-scale items; Cronbach’s α = 0.84), self-reported overall exam performance, and self-rated academic standing. Spearman correlations with 95% confidence intervals and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to examine associations. Of 103 respondents, students who used AI more frequently reported significantly greater perceived academic benefit (ρ = 0.69, 95% CI [0.57, 0.78], P < 0.001). However, AI usage frequency was not correlated with self-reported exam performance (ρ = −0.02, P = 0.81) or self-rated academic standing (ρ = −0.01, P = 0.93). Over half of students (53.4%) reported using AI Often or Always for studying. In this exploratory single-institution study, students who used AI more frequently perceived greater academic benefit, but this perception was not reflected in coarse, self-reported performance measures. This discrepancy should be interpreted cautiously and is at least as likely to reflect a measurement artifact, arising from the insensitivity of a single global performance item, recall bias, and the inability to distinguish performance before and after AI adoption, as a true gap between perception and attainment. Findings underscore the importance of helping medical students critically evaluate their AI-assisted study practices and identify priorities for more rigorous future investigation using objective, granular performance outcomes.
