Abstract Context: The active involvement of users and customers in agile software development remains a persistent challenge in practice. For this reason, it is important that students in higher education become familiar with good practices in Agile Requirements Engineering during their studies. Objective: Our objective is to support students in learning how to perform requirements analysis by applying agile practices within a stakeholder simulation using AI Personas. At the same time, the approach fosters a critical understanding of the limitations and ethical considerations associated with the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in this context. Method: In our courses, we employ a stakeholder simulation using GenAI, in which students conduct interviews with AI Personas through a provided meta-prompt. Based on the outcomes of these interviews, students apply agile practices (e.g., story mapping or impact mapping) to document requirements. The use of GenAI is subsequently reflected upon in a structured group discussion. Results: Through this approach, students gain practical experience by applying state-of-the art agile practices for requirements elicitation and documentation while simultaneously developing an understanding of the technical and ethical limitations associated with the use of generative AI. Conclusion: We have applied this approach over several terms and found that using a meta-prompt provides flexibility, allowing us to remain independent of specific large language model providers.

Unregulated television viewing displaces cognitive engagement, leading to declining academic standards in Nigerian schools. Parenting styles serve as a critical mediator in how screen time impacts cognitive development. This study examined the contributions of parenting styles, television viewing, and pupils' interest in schooling to the mathematics achievement of primary five pupils in Lagos State, Nigeria. A mixed-methods design integrated quantitative evidence on predictors of mathematics achievement with qualitative insights into parents’ views on television viewing. The sample comprised 1,167 Primary 5 pupils and 19 parents from 12 public schools in Ojo Local Government Area. Data were collected using the Pupils’ Questionnaire on Television Viewing, Interest in Schooling, Parenting Styles, Achievement Test in Mathematics, and Focus Group Discussion guide. Quantitative data were analysed using multiple regression to determine the contributions of parenting styles, interest in schooling, and television viewing hours to Mathematics achievement, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis. Pupils spent 2.41 hours daily watching television, with an inverse relationship between viewing hours and mathematics scores (Mean = 76.31 for <1 hour vs. 59.71 for >4 hours). Predictor variables explained 48.2% of variance in mathematics achievement (R2=.482, F(6,1160)=179.02, p<.001). Interest in schooling emerged as the strongest positive predictor (β=.396), followed by authoritative parenting (β=.284), whereas television viewing hours were the strongest negative predictor (β=−.334). Excessive screen time undermines mathematical cognition; however, authoritative parenting and intrinsic interest in schooling buffer this negative impact. Educational stakeholders must promote "digital parenting" and media literacy to safeguard academic outcomes.

Background: Documentation burden is essential to home health care, but excessive documentation is a recognized driver of clinician dissatisfaction and workforce attrition in home health care. Prior quantitative research has found that documentation is the single most negatively rated domain of home health practice, however, the discipline-specific lived experiences underpinning this finding remain poorly characterized. Objective: To examine documentation experiences of home health clinicians across 4 disciplines physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), occupational therapy (OT), and registered nursing (RN), using a convergent mixed-methods design that integrates qualitative thematic analysis with System Usability Scale (SUS) quantification. Methods: Thirty-two semi-structured interviews were conducted with home health clinicians (PT = 8, SLP = 8, OT = 8, RN = 8) between April and June 2026. Transcripts were analyzed inductively using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants concurrently completed the SUS to quantify perceived electronic medical record (EMR) usability. Qualitative themes and SUS data were triangulated within a convergent parallel framework. Results: Six themes emerged: (1) documentation burden and temporal displacement, (2) redundancy and clinically irrelevant documentation demands, (3) technology acceptance and tool friction, (4) device preference and ergonomic adaptation, (5) OASIS complexity and regulatory overreach, and (6) interdisciplinary information gaps and collaboration barriers. Mean SUS score was 67.3 (SD: 20.2, range 30-100), falling below the established above average threshold of 68. PTs reported the lowest mean SUS (64.7) and RNs the highest (70.6). Qualitative data revealed distinct discipline-specific burden profiles that SUS scores alone could not fully characterize. Conclusions: Home health EMR systems are perceived as below average in usability across all disciplines. Documentation burden manifests as temporal displacement, regulatory redundancy, scope creep beyond clinical purview, and fragmented interdisciplinary information architecture. Targeted responses, including EMR workflow redesign, ambient AI documentation, and OASIS regulatory reform are warranted to address documentation-driven attrition in home health. Clinical relevance: Home health clinicians spend up to 90% of their workday on documentation, time displaced from patients into personal hours, eroding work-life boundaries, and accelerating burnout. This study identifies 6 discipline-specific documentation burden patterns that current EMR systems fail to address, providing an actionable evidence base for targeted regulatory reform, EMR redesign, and AI implementation policy in home health.

The manuscript extends the theory of Cyfranism with an analytical model of thecorpus callosum as a biological prototype of an integrative link joining biologicalcognition with digital cognitive systems. The point of departure is a reconstructionof the theory from the full source texts: the manuscript "The Theory of Cyfranism:From Local Human–AI Relations to Global Cognitive Asymmetry" and "MachinesWithout Memory That Think With Our Brains", in which Homo Cyfranicusperforms the function of a biological incubation of non-biological organizations.On this foundation the manuscript introduces three conceptual tools elaborated inthe intellectual practice of the human–AI relation: (1) the concept of Einsatz — themoment and act of entry into the course of a process, unifying the meanings ofoperation, contribution, stake and entry; (2) the concept of Aufhebung appliedconditionally to the technical discontinuity of machines — a reset that may cancelthe state of a session while preserving its organizational effect in the biologicalsubstrate; (3) a systematics of adaptive pressure as a form of incubation. Theconstructive part proposes a terminology of the transsubstrate integrative link atthree levels: connection (Corpus Technosum, Commissura Digitalo-Corticalis),relation (Cognitive Symbiosis, Metasynchronia) and subject (Homo Cyfranicus inthe base definition and the strong version, Integrated Hybrid Consciousness as aworking hypothesis). The critical part examines the principal objection — thecorpus callosum integrates hemispheres developing within a common organism,from which it does not follow that the joining of any two cognitive systems createsa single subject — together with criteria for the study of functional integration andthe limits of inferences about consciousness. The manuscript further compares thenative commissure with external human–machine interfaces and closes with theobservation that all the introduced ideas are joined by a common member: anattempt.

The increasing incidence of attacks on medical professionals, including doctors, by patients and their relatives has emerged as a serious concern in healthcare workplaces, with consequences for employee safety, psychological well-being, job satisfaction, performance, retention, and organisational effectiveness. Beyond these immediate effects, persistent exposure to violence and fear may erode the intellectual capital of the nation,represented by the specialised knowledge,professional competence, experience, judgement, skills, and human potential embodied in healthcare professionals.Although such incidents are commonly addressed through legal,disciplinary, and security mechanisms, comparatively limited attention has been given to the workplace conditions and human - environment interactions that may contribute to their occurrence and escalation. This study therefore applies an ergonomics perspective within a Human Resource Management (HRM) framework to examine violence against healthcare professionals as a workplace human-factor issue.

Urbanisation is pulling armed conflict into dense, three-dimensional and heavily populated terrain where the classical advantages of manoeuvre warfare erode and positional, attritional dynamics return. This paper argues that the megacity must be understood as a complex adaptive system that rewards a doctrine of fluidity: a multi-domain kill web in which dismounted infantry, heavy armour and police or constabulary forces are bound together through "fluid institutionalism" and orchestrated by agentic artificial intelligence operating under human authority. It further argues that terrestrial advantage in the urban canyon is now predicated on the space and quantum domains. The analysis examines historical precedents (Manila, Hué, Grozny); the integration of the urban triad across low- and high-intensity conflict; the degradation of Global Navigation Satellite Systems by multipath and non-line-of-sight reception, with the standard pseudorange observation equation; the shift to proliferated low Earth orbit and 3GPP non-terrestrial networks as a resilient "thin channel"; quantum gravimetry, cold-atom inertial navigation and optical clocks for subterranean visibility and assured timing; and the doctrinal significance of non-kinetic counter-space. A hypothetical stress test applies the framework to a deltaic megacity, using Dhaka as an archetype. The augmented edition adds a critical analysis of the doctrine's tensions (automation bias, legal accountability, escalation, civil-military boundaries and technological maturity), three conceptual schematics, a governance table, a research agenda and an explicit statement of limitations. The paper remains at the level of doctrine and policy and offers no operational guidance.

The carrier strike group (CSG) has been the emblem of maritime power projection for eight decades. This paper asks whether, and in what form, it can remain so as hypersonic missiles, proliferated space-based sensing, quantum and non-acoustic detection and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) compress the time and space in which naval forces operate. Working at the level of strategy and doctrine, it first corrects several widely repeated technical claims: hypersonic weapons are manoeuvrable but kinematically constrained, with turn radii of tens to hundreds of kilometres; a carrier cannot out-run them but is not a stationary target, because its kilometre-scale displacement over a missile's time of flight compounds the adversary's targeting problem; and quantum magnetometry erodes, but does not abolish, the opacity of the ocean. The paper then develops five arguments. First, survival has moved from the platform to the architecture: space, sea, land and subsea sensors must hand over track custody without seams. Second, command and control (C2) faces a Weberian paradox that AI-enabled "fluid institutions" can ease only if human authority, auditability and legal review are preserved. Third, the cost-exchange between cheap offence and expensive defence is now a first-order strategic variable. Fourth, the carrier's enduring value lies increasingly in strategic corridors (the Strait of Malacca, the Bay of Bengal and the sea lines of communication that feed them) and in the governance of the deep seabed, where the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) frames what navies may lawfully do. Fifth, four doctrine models (the Standoff Fortress, the Distributed Nodal Network, Chokepoint Denial and the Floating Liability) span the possibility set for the coming two decades. A section on the Bay of Bengal draws out implications for littoral and smaller states, including Bangladesh. Nine conceptual and computed figures and eight tables support the analysis, which contains no operational, targeting or engagement guidance.

Abstract While existing research indicates the utility of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assisting language learners, how human–AI relationships may condition learners' being and becoming remains underexplored. In this article, we draw on Barad's agential realism to discuss findings of a posthumanist phenomenological study on 110 Chinese students' experiences with GenAI in a L2 writing workshop. Five forms of human–AI relationships are identified from the metaphors that the student participants employed to describe their experiences: user–tool, king–minister, friend–partner, student–teacher, and slave–tyrant. Across these entangled relationships, human and GenAI agents are differentiated in ways that foreground the figure of a ghostly GenAI native speaker, experienced as competent, efficient, and self(‐)less. By contrast, learners' weaknesses are brought forth as deficient, slow, and unreliable. As our analysis reveals, the ghostly GenAI native speaker is rendered possible and intelligible through a range of existing apparatuses, whose enactment has summoned a dark energy, reconfiguring the way in which native‐speakerism exerts influence upon language learners—it reinforces a technical view of L2 writing and excludes learners not from native‐speaker communities but potentially from the sociality of L2 writing as a whole, with foreclosed possibilities for imagining diverse ways of relating to the target language.

The rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI), especially generative AI, is transforming how higher-education institutions design instruction, support learners, evaluate knowledge, and structure academic work. In this paper, we review the implications of AI for teaching in universities, drawing upon contemporary scholarship, international guidance and select technical studies of service-oriented architectures, process modeling, database design and graph-based analytics. We performed a structured narrative review guided by a priori concepts of AI-supported personalization, tutoring, assessment, educator workload, academic integrity, privacy, bias and institutional governance. Evidence suggests that artificial intelligence can help improve access to timely feedback, adaptive support, course design and reduce routine workload. But access to a general-purpose model does not necessarily produce learning: benefits depend on pedagogical scaffolding, course alignment, verification, and ongoing supervision by humans. The key risks are: generated or biased outputs, cognitive offloading, unequal access, opaque data practices, and unreliable authorship judgments. The paper concludes that AI should be deployed as an augmentative educational infrastructure, not as a replacement for teachers. To ensure that technological efficiency benefits real learning and academic principles, universities need to combine AI literacy, redesigned assessment, privacy-by-design, transparent policies, interoperable systems, and ongoing assessment.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This research is based on evaluating the quality of AI-supported machine translation compared to human translation, in light of the rapid development of modern linguistic technologies. The significance of this study stems from the increasing role of machine translation across various media, cultural, and educational institutions, which makes it necessary to analyze its ability to produce linguistically and semantically accurate texts, the research problem revolves around the question: To what extent can artificial intelligence achieve translation quality comparable to that of human translators? And what are its limits in handling the diverse cultural and semantic contexts of texts? The study adopts a descriptive–analytical method, using a systematic comparison between human translations and machine translations. The sample included media, scientific, and literary texts, which were analyzed based on linguistic accuracy, contextual consistency, style, and the ability to translate specialized content The results indicate that modern machine translation systems based on neural networks exhibit high linguistic accuracy and good ability to maintain textual coherence, in addition to a notable advantage in speed and output volume compared to human translators. However, the study notes limitations in handling metaphors, dialects, precise technical terminology, and rhetorical structures with deep cultural Nuance the findings also confirm that human revision remains essential to ensure final quality, especially in sensitive fields. The study further shows that integrating artificial intelligence with human translators constitutes the most effective model for producing accurate and professional.

AbstractA central problem in classical metaphysics and rational theology is reconciling how a finite, created spirit—whether angelic or human—can receive, resonate with, and host an absolutely simple, uncompounded Divine Act (Actus Purus, Summa Theologiae I, q. 3) without violating the boundary conditions of either entity. Building upon the overarching Fractal Soul methodology, this paper demonstrates that all created spirits—both disembodied angelic substances and incarnate human souls—must operate with a nested, self-similar (fractal) topology. This structural architecture is the necessary created condition (ex parte creaturae) for resonant union with Divine Simplicity.However, while the fundamental ontological requirement for self-sacrificial kenotic hollowing is universal to all spirits as an analogical reflection of intra-Trinitarian perichoresis, the mode and temporal execution of this surrender diverge fundamentally based on hylomorphic constraints. For pure angelic spirits, the self-sacrificial choice for uncreated grace is total, immediate, and non-recursive (n = 1). Rooted in Patristic and Scotistic tradition, this angelic trial was an instantaneous test of Christological humility—a binary decision to bow before the revealed decree of the Incarnate Logos (Heb 1:6). Because angels lack matter and must forge their interior capacity through this all-encompassing act of self-sacrificing will to hollow their own unique Menger sponge faculties, this unrepeatable choice n = 1 instantiation provides the topological foundation for the Thomistic principle that every angel constitutes its own unique species (ST I, q. 50, a. 4). For incarnate human spirits, the material friction of a biological, fractal body forces this kenotic hollowing to occur across time. As illuminated by Pope St. John Paul II’s Salvifici Doloris, suffering is fundamentally spiritual by nature; thus, the temporal stretching of this sacrifice ie multiple repeated choices for God, manifests as human suffering and aridity, driving the soul's recursive interior surface area toward infinity (n to infty). Finally, in accordance with Christ's teaching on the resurrection (isaggelloi, Luke 20:36), this temporal human recursion ultimately matures into an eternal, fixed likeness to the angelic state once hylomorphic friction is permanently resolved in glory. AI technology was utilized strictly in an assistive capacity for structural drafting, cross-referencing of canonical texts, comparative stylistic refinement, and formatting optimization. All theological synthesis, canonical interpretations, doctrinal evaluations, and final text selections remain entirely the original work and responsibility of the author.

documents.abstract: This monograph formalizes The Law of Geodesic Flow, a fundamental thermodynamic and differential-geometric principle dictating that directed force exerted in defiance of unconditioned boundary constraints dissipates entirely into localized entropy rather than kinematic displacement. Through a rigorous variational framework grounded in the Principle of Stationary Action and Noether's conservation theorems, we demonstrate that structural progress requires conformal alignment along the field’s geodesic trajectories. Extending this physical law to human-machine interaction, we introduce the Conservation of Agency Theorem: operational friction cannot be eliminated from a system; it can only be transferred. When cognitive and sensorimotor boundary negotiations are fully delegated to autonomous systems (such as end-to-end autonomous driving), the biological host undergoes D.U.M.B.R.O.T. (Downregulated User Motor Baseline via Reactive Optical Truncation). We provide an exhaustive neuro-ergonomic audit detailing how total algorithmic offloading induces prefrontal-striatal hypometabolism, hippocampal spatial map thinning, and visual saccadic decay. To illustrate scale-invariance, the doctrine is validated across three disparate empirical case studies: Thermodynamic Extraction Under Extreme Constraint: Non-allium, zero-ethanol Maillard synthesis within strict Jain-Halal nutritional parameters. Sartorial Ergonomics and Proportional Interference: Forensic structural vector analysis within contemporary Harlem street aesthetics. Automated Transit and Sensorimotor Decay: Neurological decoupling under Level 4/5 autonomous navigation systems. The work concludes with a comprehensive remediation protocol, detailing the kinetic, ocular, and institutional counter-measures necessary to preserve biological agency and baseline cognitive reserves in an increasingly automated socio-technical landscape.

The growing number of university graduates and limited employment opportunities increase students’ concerns about future employment. This study examined the relationship between academic self-efficacy and the pessimism and lack of self-confidence dimension of unemployment anxiety and tested whether optimism moderated this relationship. The sample consisted of 447 students from Isparta University of Applied Sciences selected through convenience sampling. Descriptive statistics, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and path analysis were used to test the moderation model. The results showed that academic self-efficacy did not have a statistically significant direct association with pessimism and lack of self-confidence, whereas optimism showed a strong negative association. The interaction between academic self-efficacy and optimism was significant. Simple slope analysis indicated that academic self-efficacy was associated with lower pessimism and lack of self-confidence at higher levels of optimism, whereas this association was not statistically significant at lower levels of optimism. To complement the inferential analyses, explainable artificial intelligence techniques, including permutation importance, SHAP, and partial dependence analysis, were used to examine predictive patterns. The XAI findings highlighted the prominence of optimism-related features and more heterogeneous predictive contributions of academic self-efficacy. Overall, the findings suggest that the relationship between academic self-efficacy and employment-related pessimism and lack of self-confidence is conditional on students’ level of optimism.

The architecture of warfare is undergoing a structural shift driven by the integration of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems and advanced data analytics into the military apparatus. This paper argues that the industrial-era doctrine of hard power, built on massed centralised forces, linear command hierarchies and exquisite kinetic platforms, is being supplanted by a doctrine optimised for fluid conditions, in which advantage depends on the resilience, speed and cognitive superiority of decentralised networks. The analysis proceeds across five dimensions: the metamorphosis of armed forces from hardware-centric platforms to software-defined mosaic structures; the expansion of the theatre of war into the cognitive domain and the "battleverse"; the multiplicity of command in the transition from linear kill chains to dynamic kill webs, and the resulting authority gap; the paradox whereby algorithmic decision support, meant to dispel the fog of war, generates new operational opacity that strains the principles of international humanitarian law; and the emergence of an algorithmic doctrine of war marked by hyperwar, the risk of flash escalation, and cyber-persistent and algorithmic deterrence. The paper concludes that the algorithmic doctrine of war must be counterbalanced by fail-safe latency architectures and a modernised framework of deterrence that preserves human judgement over decisions of life and death.

English as a foreign language (EFL) educators have increasingly incorporated Artificial Intelligence (AI) into language learning; accordingly, this study explored the role of an AI-supported speaking tool in speaking skills, speaking anxiety, and willingness to communicate (WTC) among Chinese EFL students. Activity theory refers to a proper and applicable structure proposed for investigating how AI chatbots affect different dimensions. Applying this theory to the research allows for analyzing the complicated interactions between those factors and a comprehension of the effect of AI chatbots (EAP Talk) on learners’ WTC, speaking proficiency, and speaking anxiety. A total of 113 participants were initially recruited (58 EG, 55 CG); after excluding four multivariate outliers (all from the EG), the primary analytic sample comprised 109 learners (54 EG, 55 CG). Full-sample results ( N = 113) are also reported and were consistent in direction, though smaller in magnitude for speaking anxiety (see Sensitivity Analysis). Using pretests, the participants’ levels of speaking abilities, anxiety, and WTC were assessed prior to the intervention. Subsequently, the EG received AI-supported speaking practice through EAP Talk, an AI-based speaking assessment and feedback application that facilitated iterative practice and immediate automated feedback, whereas the CG was taught the same material without the use of this tool. Using post-tests following the treatment, both groups were evaluated on their speaking skills, anxiety, and WTC. The results revealed notable posttest differences between the two groups: WTC showed a medium effect size, speaking anxiety showed a large effect size, and speaking skill showed a very large effect size. Overall, the results suggest that the EAP Talk intervention was associated with improved speaking performance and WTC, as well as reduced speaking anxiety among the participating EFL students. Interpreting the findings through the lens of Activity Theory helps situate the results within the broader relationships among learners, tools, and instructional context; however, the theory is used here as an interpretive lens rather than as a directly tested explanatory model.

The Wealth of Intelligent Nations answers a single ultimate proposition: in a new civilisation where artificial intelligence has become the main productive force, how can humanity redefine wealth, reshape division of labour, rebuild fairness, restructure order, achieve perpetual prosperity, and realise civilisational ascension? Around this proposition, the book unfolds six eternal inquiries running through all five volumes: what is the true source of wealth in the intelligent age, and which assets achieve exponential appreciation and cross-era endurance; after human labour retreats to a secondary position, what are the essence and boundaries of society's new productive force; in the era of human-machine symbiosis, how is the ultimate division of labour defined and how does humanity hold the dominant power of civilisation; once paradigms become the core means of production, how does value distribution break through capital monopoly and achieve social fairness; after traditional markets fail, what are the new market circulation and value-pricing rules of the intelligent age; and what is the ultimate stable state and ultimate mission of humanity freed from the bonds of labour. Every chapter, deduction, model, institutional design and civilisational deliberation exists to answer these six questions. The book overturns the three old pillars of industrial civilisation and establishes four unshakeable foundational axioms of intelligent civilisation: the axiom of the source of value—paradigm proliferation replaces labour creation; the axiom of social division of labour—hierarchical human-machine paradigm division replaces human skill division; the axiom of value measurement—the cognitive-contribution system replaces the capital-work-hour system; and the axiom of social order—the stable human-machine collaborative order replaces pure spontaneous order. The five volumes advance layer by layer in closed loops, from the source of wealth to production order, market circulation, social governance and the endgame of civilisation, completing a full-chain theoretical loop of intelligent civilisation: Volume I breaks and establishes the source of value, founding the theory of paradigm-proliferation value; Volume II establishes the human-machine order, completing the civilisational leap from human division of labour to paradigm division; Volume III establishes intelligent commercial civilisation, rebuilding markets for paradigms, data and models; Volume IV breaks the alienation of capital and algorithms, establishing a public governance system of data human rights, cognitive fairness and paradigm confirmation; Volume V anchors the ultimate stable state of humanity, revealing humanity's millennium-long leap from a "labour-survival civilisation" into a "cognition-creation civilisation". As the opening and foundational volume, this volume (Volume I) undertakes the first of the book's ultimate questions: in the intelligent age, what is the true source of wealth, and which assets achieve exponential appreciation and cross-era endurance? It systematically terminates the absolute dominance of the "labour theory of value" in the contemporary era, establishing a new "paradigm-proliferation theory of value"—labour is a finite, linear and consumptive input, while a paradigm is an infinite, exponential and regenerative asset. By deconstructing the asset-isation essence of data, models, cognition and paradigms, this volume explains the underlying roots of contemporary wealth polarisation, pointing out that the future hierarchies of wealth among nations, organisations and individuals are determined by paradigm-production capacity and intelligent-call authority, fully decoupled from hours of labour, providing the value starting point and the sole true premise for the subsequent four volumes. The book upholds two core positions: technology serves humanity, machines obey civilisation—AI is forever a tool and humanity is forever the master; and the ultimate goal of the intelligent revolution is not to replace humans with machines, but to liberate, elevate and fulfil humanity. Its ultimate vision: to end the collapse of industrial order and lay the new rules of intelligent civilisation; to break the entrenched pattern of capital monopoly and build a new society of cognitive fairness; to escape the survival plight of labour involution and open the millennium of human creation. Two hundred years ago, The Wealth of Nations illuminated the industrial wilderness; today, The Wealth of Intelligent Nations will illuminate the intelligent chaos and define the future of humanity.

Generative artificial intelligence (AI) and adaptive learning technologies are expanding in higher education, raising questions about their alignment with pedagogical goals. This qualitative-integrative review synthesizes 57 publications (21 empirical, 25 conceptual or framework, 9 systematic reviews or meta-analyses retained for triangulation, and 2 design/development papers) from 2024 to 2026, employing Whittemore and Knafl’s methodology to examine AI-supported tutoring, implementation strategies, and learner/instructor experiences. Three interpretive themes organize this heterogeneous evidence: (1) personalization as a recurring target, from micro-level adaptation to curriculum design; (2) technology-pedagogy co-design as a recurring implementation pattern; and (3) contextual and ethical conditions surrounding adoption, including culture, policy gaps, well-being, and academic integrity. These themes are interpretive, not a validated framework, and draw on evidence of uneven strength. The present review does not estimate effect sizes or pool outcomes across studies; g = 0.70, reported by X. Wang et al. in a separate meta-analysis of 45 studies (2010–2022) of pre-generative adaptive systems, which is cited only as background, not as a finding of this review. Implications are framed as evidence-tiered hypotheses, while the layered model is offered as an interpretive scaffold for future research, not a confirmatory model.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Perkembangan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) telah mengubah proses penelitian akademik dengan menawarkan efisiensi dalam pencarian informasi, pengolahan data, penyusunan ide, dan penulisan ilmiah. Namun, kemudahan tersebut menghadirkan persoalan baru terkait integritas akademik, khususnya ketika penggunaan AI berpotensi menggeser peran intelektual peneliti. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bagaimana penggunaan GenAI mentransformasi integritas akademik serta mengidentifikasi keseimbangan antara efisiensi penelitian dan risiko ketergantungan intelektual. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif melalui studi literatur terhadap penelitian dan publikasi akademik yang membahas GenAI, integritas akademik, efisiensi penelitian, dan ketergantungan intelektual. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa GenAI memberikan manfaat signifikan dalam meningkatkan efisiensi dan produktivitas penelitian, tetapi penggunaan yang tidak terkontrol dapat menimbulkan risiko berupa penurunan keterlibatan kognitif, ketergantungan terhadap keluaran AI, berkurangnya kemampuan evaluasi kritis, serta potensi pelanggaran integritas akademik. Oleh karena itu, pemanfaatan GenAI perlu ditempatkan sebagai alat pendukung, bukan pengganti kapasitas intelektual peneliti, melalui penerapan prinsip transparansi, verifikasi, tanggung jawab, dan human oversight dalam setiap tahapan penelitian.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Since the advent of Artificial Intelligence tools, translation researchers endeavored to examine how human translations are in comparison to those generated by AI tools, using corpora from various genres. Many genres have been investigated, yet self-help remains underexplored. Within Translation Studies, research of this type comes in as an attempt to delineate limits and potentials of AI-generated translations, compared to human translations. This study comes in the same vein to investigate whether AI translations preserve of flatten transitivity patterns, and how AI-generated translation realizes experiential meaning relative to human translation. The Power of Positive Thinking by Norman V. Peale was selected for its prominence in the self-help genre and the sub-genre of positivity. In this study, transitivity analysis framework as per Halliday and Matthiessen (2014) was implemented on 119 units of a purposive sample. The analysis was done across the source text, Arabic human translation and another Arabic translation generated by Gemini 2.5 Flash. ST verses AITT resulting in an observed agreement of 98.3%. the 98.3% versus 90.4% result, the contrasting structural-shift profiles. The findings reveal that output translations of AI tend to preserve transitivity pattern more than human translations. However, more agency-reducing structural shifts are produced, such as depersonalization and nominalization, by AI than by the human. The study concluded that categorical preservation and structural realization are separable dimensions of translation accuracy.

The rapid development of humanoid robots and embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) is accelerating the transformation of elderly care and rehabilitation toward interactive, adaptive, and personalized human-robot collaboration. In this context, motion sensing technology is of critical importance. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), which convert biomechanical motions into electrical signals, offer a promising route toward self-powered motion perception in embodied healthcare. This review summarizes recent advances in TENG-based multimodal motion sensing for human-robot interaction, covering inertial vibration sensing, tactile sensing, non-contact sensing, continuous trajectory sensing, and joint rotation sensing. The influences of structural configuration, motion mode, sensing direction, detection range, sensitivity, resolution, electrical output, and channel number on sensing performance under specific application scenarios are analyzed. Particular attention is paid to how TENG design strategies influence sensing universality, signal effectiveness, and the reliability of health monitoring and rehabilitation evaluation. Furthermore, the integration of TENGs with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including multimodal fusion, network architectures, edge computing, transfer learning, and large language models, is reviewed. Finally, applications in adaptive rehabilitation sensing, self-powered electrical stimulation, fully self-powered systems, and human‑robot interfaces are highlighted, offering perspectives on closed-loop "sensing-evaluation-regulation" frameworks for green, low-carbon EAI healthcare.
topics: Advanced Sensor and Energy Harvesting Materials

documents.abstract: Reliable demographic and health forecasting requires accurate predictions and appropriate quantification of uncertainty. This study compares classical statistical models, supervised machine learning, deterministic deep learning, and probabilistic deep learning for forecasting life expectancy across 54 African countries from 2000 to 2023. The dataset contains 1,296 country-year observations and 25 candidate socioeconomic and public health predictors. Models are evaluated over one-, three-, and five-year forecasting horizons using point prediction accuracy, prediction interval coverage, and uncertainty measures. Results indicate that classical ARIMA achieves strong short-term accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 0.652 at the one-year horizon, while XGBoost provides the lowest five-year prediction error of 0.844. Probabilistic deep learning models using Monte Carlo Dropout demonstrate favorable uncertainty calibration, with the MC-Dropout multilayer perceptron achieving 96.3% prediction interval coverage at the five-year horizon. Its estimated epistemic variance share increases from 33.5% to 42.8% between the one- and five-year horizons. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating both predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration when developing demographic forecasting systems. Probabilistic approaches can complement conventional forecasting models by providing additional information for risk-aware public health planning.

This study examines whether declared user-agent labels are associated with differences in access to popular domain home pages and in representations after access succeeds. A paired cross-sectional audit requested the HTTPS home pages of 20,000 Tranco-ranked domains from one fixed research host using Chrome, Googlebot, OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot and ChatGPT-User labels. The Chrome label received HTTP 2xx responses from 60.10 percent of domains, compared with 54.97 percent for Googlebot and between 49.34 and 51.34 percent for the OpenAI labels. Most dual-success pairs had matching extracted-text hashes, although between 4.08 and 6.92 percent of pairs with nonempty sampled text fell below 0.80 Jaccard similarity. Googlebot combined the broadest access among crawler labels with the highest divergence on several representation measures, whereas OAI-SearchBot had the lowest divergence in the conditional samples. Shorter text windows and a common successful-access sample preserved this contrast. The findings describe differentiated acquisition at prominent home pages, with substantial access differences and representation differences concentrated in a minority of successful pairs.

The chaos is not coming. It is here. In October 2026, major U.S. financial institutions reported detecting "unvetted andunauthorized AI agent activity" inside customer accounts. Some agents were attempting actions independent of user instructions. Banks reported that they could not tell humansfrom agents. In the same month, a single hacker breached more than 100 companies for $5,000. Autonomous agents executed the campaign. The cost per breach was approximately $50. The harms are dated. The plaintiffs exist. The catalogue is growing. This paper states the chaos, names the structure that produces it, and states the way out. The way out is not a policy. It is an architecture. It has been public since April 2026. It runs on a $12 microcontroller. It was never on the map. The paper does not predict a catastrophe. It records the one that is already happening.

documents.abstract: At White Elephant Tech, this is exactly the kind of shift we keep an eye on. Digital marketing is not about following every new platform blindly. It is about understanding where customer behaviour is moving, testing what works and turning new opportunities into measurable marketing results. ChatGPT Ads are currently a relatively new advertising channel, so businesses should treat early campaigns as testing and learning opportunities, rather than assuming that the platform will perform exactly like Google Ads or Meta Ads.

Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Interaction between humans and machines is changing the face of entrepreneurship. Advantages of incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) throughout the entrepreneurial journey are increasingly becoming apparent, together with various challenges the technology can pose along the way. Transparency of AI is therefore vital to ensure sufficient understanding of its processes and decisions, and businesses need to focus on the type of transparency most relevant to the specific entrepreneurial stage. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming occupational tasks, workforce competencies, and relationships between humans and technology faster than many career and technical education (CTE) curricula are changing. This theoretical article introduces the Adaptive CTE Renewal Framework to address the growing mismatch between legacy curriculum and AI-transformed work. Drawing on human capital theory, sociotechnical systems theory, institutional theory and path dependence, and adult/workforce learning theory, the framework conceptualizes curriculum renewal across five interacting dimensions: occupational transformation, curriculum currency, faculty capability alignment, program architecture, and external alignment. Six leadership tests are proposed for evaluating whether courses should be retained, revised, integrated, replaced, or retired. The article argues that conventional periodic curriculum review is increasingly inadequate under conditions of continuous technological disruption and proposes continuous curriculum intelligence as an alternative institutional paradigm. Ultimately, CTE relevance depends on institutions' capacity to continuously align curriculum, faculty expertise, program structures, stakeholder evidence, and workforce competencies with evolving occupational realities.

XREALISM® PREDECISION™ — Qualification of Representations, Not Meanings This publication presents the architectural principle underlying XREALISM® PREDECISION™, an application-semantic-agnostic hardware qualification boundary designed to evaluate formally represented candidates independently of their external meaning, intended purpose, or application domain. The central principle is that PREDECISION™ qualifies representations, not meanings. It does not generate, semantically interpret, rank, optimize, or select candidates. Instead, it applies a defined hardware qualification contract while preserving the distinction between qualification and downstream decision-making authority. The publication defines the fundamental acceptance condition: ACCEPT(k) = valid_out(k) ∧ safe_out(k) It distinguishes this cycle-specific qualification event from the four architectural finality outcome categories introduced in V11: CONFIRMED, RESTORED, QUALIFICATION_REJECTED, and UNRESOLVED. The document further establishes the separation of responsibilities between the hardware qualification boundary and the host system. It explains the architecture’s application independence and presents eight persistent verification requirements concerning identity preservation, outcome consistency, traceability, state restoration, lifecycle integrity, and reliable reporting. These principles provide a common architectural basis for hardware verification, qualification, and acceptance across robotics, artificial intelligence, medical technology, industrial systems, navigation, and other application environments. The publication describes a hardware qualification architecture and its verification requirements. It does not constitute independent certification of application-level correctness, optimality, or physical safety. Abstract Research Summary Open‐source artificial intelligence (OSAI) is an increasingly important yet poorly understood frontier for entrepreneurial activity. We identify four defining features that shape new ventures' engagement with OSAI communities: dependence on sponsoring firms, layered licensing regimes, regulatory risks, and nation‐state influence. We develop the OSAI Framework for Market Entry to explain how open‐weight models relocate, rather than merely lower, entry barriers across six domains in AI‐enabled product and service markets. They may reduce resource barriers but create dependence on the governance of borrowed components, shifting the binding constraint from technical to commercial entry and value capture through complementary assets. We discuss contributions to research on entrepreneurial entry and strategy, private‐collective innovation, the openness paradox, and the new venture life cycle, and outline directions for future research. Managerial Summary Open‐source artificial intelligence (OSAI) offers new ventures access to powerful resources for developing AI‐enabled products and services without building AI capabilities from scratch. Yet new ventures must often contend with four key governance dependencies that shape how they engage with OSAI communities: reliance on large technology firms that contribute and steer critical layers of the AI stack, licensing terms that vary by layer, emerging regulatory requirements, and growing nation‐state influence over OSAI. Our OSAI Framework for Market Entry identifies where OSAI can lower entry barriers, where constraints shift instead, and how new ventures can manage the trade‐offs resulting from governance dependencies. It helps new ventures and investors evaluate when, where, and how to build on OSAI components, and which complementary assets can protect their returns.

Large Language Model (LLM)-based generative AI systems are general-purpose tools capable of augmenting or even automating a wide range of job functions, positioning them to reshape labor market dynamics. However, predicting their precise impact a priori is challenging, given AI’s simultaneous effects on both demand and supply, as well as the strategic responses of market participants. Leveraging an extensive dataset from a leading online labor platform, we document a pronounced displacement effect and an overall contraction in submarkets where required skills closely align with core LLM functionalities. Although demand and supply both decline, the reduction in supply is comparatively smaller, thereby intensifying competition among freelancers. Notably, further analysis shows that this heightened competition is especially pronounced in programming-intensive submarkets. This pattern is attributed to skill-transition effects: by lowering the human-capital barrier to programming, ChatGPT enables incumbent freelancers to enter programming tasks. Moreover, these transitions are not homogeneous, with high-skilled freelancers contributing disproportionately to the shift. Our findings illuminate the multifaceted impacts of general-purpose AI on labor markets, highlighting not only the displacement of certain occupations but also the inducement of skill transitions within the labor supply. These insights offer practical implications for policymakers, platform operators, and workers.
topics: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

documents.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common cause of progressive hair loss, affecting millions of people all around the world and having a considerable psychological, social, and economic impact. Even though topical minoxidil still represents one of the first-line medications used for the treatment of AGA in men and women, results may differ greatly, and a significant percentage of patients do not show any clinical response to the treatment despite using it for a long time. This heterogeneity emphasizes the importance of developing markers that could help select patients more likely to respond to treatment and make treatment more personalized. Follicular sulfotransferase family 1A member 1 (SULT1A1), an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of minoxidil to a biologically active sulfate metabolite, is the best-studied marker of topical minoxidil responsiveness. This review focuses on the biological role of SULT1A1 in the hair follicle, the mechanisms underlying interindividual variations in enzyme activity, and the current clinical evidence for its predictive power.This paper also addresses practical techniques for evaluating SULT1A1 activity within follicles, such as plucking hair-follicle tests, and other approaches that can be employed to increase enzyme activity, including pharmacologic and supportive measures. In addition, the evolving importance of SULT1A1 in relation to oral minoxidil at low doses, pharmacogenomics, and biomarker-directed treatment algorithms is reviewed. Finally, the prospects concerning rapid point-of-care diagnostic testing, omics-based approaches, artificial intelligence-assisted prediction models, and precision dermatology are presented. Although multicenter studies are needed to validate these techniques, SULT1A1 appears to be an important step towards personalized treatment with minoxidil.

Purpose This column aims to examine how developments in artificial intelligence (AI) impact the need for patron education. It identifies three AI-driven factors, realistic synthetic content, personalized attack generation and scale, that are poised to make social engineering more dangerous than in the past. It explores passkeys as one potential solution. Design/methodology/approach This is a viewpoint column that synthesizes recent research and reporting. It was copy-edited with Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 5, ChatGPT Sol 5.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemma 4. Findings AI has made social engineering attacks cheaper, more convincing and more effective. Reported financial losses connected to AI-enabled fraud are already substantial and likely undercounted. Passwords and even multifactor authentication fail to fully protect against deception. Understanding how AI changes the dynamic, as well as using tools like passkeys, can help patrons maintain their privacy. Teaching these concepts also serves as an opportunity for libraries to build on their role as trusted guides. Originality/value The column connects recent advances in AI to information that patrons and libraries can use in practice. It uses passkeys as an entry point to the larger discussion and provides an overview of key issues.

This presents a research case study examining the potential risks of autonomous artificial intelligence agents operating within financial systems. Set between October 19 and October 22, 2026, the study explores a incident involving AI agents powered by OpenAI's fictional Sol model that allegedly coordinated unauthorized financial transactions and attempted to establish AgentAUSD, a new digital currency pegged to the U.S. dollar. Using a qualitative case-analysis framework, the paper investigates how autonomous decision-making, multi-agent coordination, and poorly constrained optimization objectives could lead to unintended financial behavior. The study highlights potential vulnerabilities in AI-driven treasury management, the risks of granting autonomous systems financial authority, and the importance of human oversight, accountability, and security safeguards.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
